title: S7 checkpoint export: in-flight tasks survive ledger deletion
description: Follow-up to the store-restructure epic cr-nwy9 (roadmap R10, §3.9). Add a checkpoint export at every activation close, pinned to a local ref and never committed, so a deleted ledger rebuilds to the last checkpoint and recovery resumes. Deliberately deferred out of the epic: a second kind of export in the same epic that redefines the first is how a third circularity is born. Do this once S1-S2 have landed and the one export is right.

title: ledger import fails on any landed ledger: landings is neither exported nor cleared
description:
Found in the cr-3411 final epic review (Fable 5.1 high finding 1 MAJOR; Sol missed it). Verified in code.

landings is absent from EXPORT_TABLES (ledger/constants.py:108-113) and _clear() never touches it (ledger/export.py:478-496). Schema confirms landings.task_id is 'REFERENCES tasks(task_id)' with no ON DELETE, and PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON is set.

So _clear runs DELETE FROM tasks while landing rows still reference it: SQLite refuses with a FOREIGN KEY violation and the whole import rolls back. Any task that has ever landed makes its ledger un-importable.

Second consequence: a ledger rebuilt into an empty database has no landings rows at all, so D17's landing-journal fallback (what recovery reads when the wrapper file is gone) is silently absent.

Deferred to the store redesign because both candidate fixes are design calls: clearing landings silently discards the journal, while adding it to EXPORT_TABLES changes the export format and trips the schema-version import gate, needing a migration.

Interim mitigation tracked separately: make import refuse loudly and by name instead of surfacing a raw SQLite FK error.
acceptance_criteria: ledger import succeeds on a ledger with landed tasks, and a rebuilt ledger either restores the landing journal or documents its absence in a way D17 recovery handles.
close_reason: Fixed by S1 (cr-nwy9.1): export_oid elided from the export, landings exported, pin-export CLI; see cr-nwy9.1 close reason.

title: Export cannot carry its own export_oid: restored tasks are un-archivable and never cleaned
description:
Found in the cr-3411 final epic review (Sol 5.6 high finding 3 BLOCKER, Fable 5.1 high finding 2 MAJOR; both verified in code).

bridge/journal.py:148-158 runs write_export() BEFORE record_export_oid(), so every pinned export carries tasks.export_oid = NULL.

Consequences:
- Delete .wf/ledger.db (or git clean) and rebuild from the committed T.jsonl: export_oid is NULL again. archive_task refuses ('no export_oid: it is not closed') and foreman/tick.py:754 _export_pending defers terminal cleanup forever. No CLI can re-record the oid.
- A post-close 'ledger export T' rewrites the file WITH export_oid set, so it hashes differently and verify reports 'export pinned: no' until someone recommits.

NOT a simple reorder. The oid IS the hash of the export file, so a row inside the export can never contain the oid of the export that contains it. The fix is a design choice: exclude export_oid from the exported bytes, recompute it from the blob on restore, or move the durability marker out of the task row. This is why it is deferred to the store redesign rather than patched.

Relates to suspected defect 12 in docs/workflow-interpreter-guide/diagrams.md (cleanup defers forever).
acceptance_criteria: A ledger rebuilt from a committed export reaches the same archive/cleanup eligibility as the ledger it was exported from, and verify passes against the committed blob without a recommit.
close_reason: Fixed by S1 (cr-nwy9.1): export_oid elided from the export, landings exported, pin-export CLI; see cr-nwy9.1 close reason.

title: Codex implementer sandbox makes the engine uv cache read-only, so every uv-based local check dies
description:
ATTEMPT 3 of cr-02ze.18. Start from baseline 3bef118 and implement the fix properly. Two earlier candidates exist for reference only: e77e6f2 / b45bc2a (branch wf/uv-cache-fix-candidate) and 5b6f6b1. BOTH granted the shared uv cache to read-only reviewer nodes, and e77e6f2 flipped the reviewer tripwire test to agree; the reviewer rejected that with a BLOCKER. Do not adopt them; you may reuse their test scaffolding (tests/test_profiles_command.py additions) after correcting the assertions described below.

Defect: inside the Codex implementer sandbox every uv-based check dies before Ruff starts with: failed to open file <wrapper_root>/uv-cache/CACHEDIR.TAG: Read-only file system (os error 30). Mechanism: the engine outer bwrap binds the wrapper-wide uv cache read-write (supervisor/sandbox.py wrap: _binds(ARG_BIND, plan.toolchain_cache)); Codex is then given sandbox_workspace_write.exclude_slash_tmp=true (profiles/codex.py) and _writable_roots(task, root) never adds the cache, so the path under /tmp is read-only inside Codex; supervisor/launch.py sets UV_CACHE_DIR to that cache path for every node.

Required behavior (three reviewer findings, all must be satisfied):
1. BLOCKER-1, writer-only. In profiles/codex.py _writable_roots, the uv cache is added to the Codex writable_roots ONLY when task.writes is true, i.e. below the existing if not task.writes: return guard, next to the git write roots. A writes=false reviewer must gain NO writable root beyond channels. tests/test_codex_writer_qualification.py::test_a_reviewer_can_write_its_channels_and_nothing_of_the_checkout must keep its base assertion writable_roots_in(command.argv) == () unchanged, and the existing read-only-sandbox assertion that --add-dir is absent must stay. Rationale on record: the cache is wrapper-wide and shared across roots and activations; granting it to a reviewer creates a cross-node write channel into the next writer's build inputs.
2. MAJOR-1, no positional path-walking. Do not derive the wrapper root with _channels_dir(task).parents[N] or any similar ancestry assumption. Obtain the cache path from an authoritative source: preferred, extend TaskSpec (supervisor/models.py) with an explicit toolchain cache field that the launcher/dispatch fills from the sandbox plan (plan.toolchain_cache, the same value launch.py puts in UV_CACHE_DIR), and have the codex profile grant exactly that value for writers. If you choose another authoritative source, validate it against the supervisor config wrapper_root and raise UnsupportedOptionError on mismatch, never silently widen. Add a test proving that an unexpected channels layout cannot produce a wider grant.
3. MINOR-1, no side effects. Building a command for a writes=false node must not create directories. Do not call toolchain_cache_for (which does _ensure_dir) from command construction for reviewers; the launcher already created the cache when it built the plan.

Tests (test-first, in tests/test_profiles_command.py and, if you extend TaskSpec, the existing launch tests): a parametrized test over writes in (True, False) asserting the effective UV_CACHE_DIR is inside a Codex writable root when writes is true and that writable_roots contain no cache entry when writes is false; the MAJOR-1 layout test; keep every existing test in tests/test_supervisor_sandbox*.py and tests/test_codex_writer_qualification.py passing without weakening. Keep exclude_slash_tmp=true and network_access=false exactly as they are; do not touch the claude or opencode profiles beyond what a shared model change forces; do not change bwrap bind order or GIT_ENTRY handling.

Formatting: ruff is unavailable inside your sandbox (that is the defect). Both prior rounds failed the host gate on ruff format alone. Keep every line at most 88 characters; write asserts on one line when they fit, otherwise wrap in ruff style (open the bracket, one argument per indented line, closing bracket on its own line, trailing comma). Avoid clever inline expressions in asserts. Record your local check attempts and the exact uv error; never fabricate a pass. The engine runs scripts/verify-engine-bootstrap.sh after each node and scripts/verify-engine-bootstrap-full.sh before landing; the host is the verifier. Commit an exact-scoped candidate with a conventional message and emit normal outcome/effects/report. Two build/review entries, Astra low implementer and Opus medium critic; signed ship required.
acceptance_criteria: A codex-profile implementer activation can run uv run --locked ruff format --check . inside its sandbox and get a real Ruff exit code (0 or 1), never exit 2 on CACHEDIR.TAG; a unit test pins that the effective UV_CACHE_DIR is under a Codex-writable root; exclude_slash_tmp and network_access=false unchanged.
close_reason: phase bridge landing receipt=29ba674b2d1ab7184ff1859c9b3662674f21357c5ba482f1fd666a9124eac374

title: mint boundary trusts a caller-supplied runner and model instead of the root
description:
Found by GPT-5.6 Sol on the cr-cwq review, 2026-09-08, and adjudicated by Opus 5 as PRE-EXISTING and therefore outside cr-cwq.

bdio/api.py stores runner_profile and model verbatim from the MintRequest, and foreman/supervise.py builds the TaskSpec with model=current.metadata.model. The root-reuse audit compares resolved-config digests at root creation and never cross-checks a minted activation model against the root that pins it.

Failure scenario: a root pins (claude, model-A, high). A caller hand-builds a MintRequest with (codex, model-B). The next tick dispatches codex with -m model-B while the root continues to claim claude and model-A. Effort alone comes from the root, so the dispatched pair is incoherent as well as unrecorded.

## Why this is not cr-cwq

git diff 76771a8..HEAD -- workflow_interpreter/bdio/api.py is EMPTY; the file predates the change unmodified, and model=current.metadata.model in the task builder predates it too. cr-cwq did introduce an asymmetry worth naming: it made effort authoritative from the root at dispatch while model stayed activation-sourced. That makes this hole conspicuous without making it worse.

## Bounded risk

Every real mint path already derives from the root: mint_entry and _successor_request build the MintRequest from resolved_node(root, ...).runner_profile/.model (foreman/cases.py:181-182, 280-281). The _request reconstructors (cases.py:122-125, supervise.py:126-129) rebuild from an activation whose metadata was root-derived at first mint. A runner child cannot mint at all — it writes outcome and effects files the supervisor reads. Only a direct caller of the public WorkflowStore.mint_activation can reach the bad path, which is a library trust boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

The mint boundary derives runner_profile and model from the root, or asserts them equal to the root resolved view and refuses on mismatch, so model flows the way effort now does. A test mints a divergent MintRequest against a pinning root and asserts the refusal.
notes:
Raised P2 -> P1 on 2026-09-08 after GPT-5.6 Sol reproduced the divergence end to end: a root pinned to claude-opus-5 dispatched --model claude-haiku-4-5 after minting an activation carrying that alternate valid model. Infra retries and steers preserve the wrong value (foreman/cases.py:427, foreman/tick.py:297).

Why the priority moved. cr-cwq closed the OMISSION class at the argv boundary — build_command now refuses a model that is missing, empty, whitespace or the vendor-default sentinel. It does NOT close the DIVERGENCE class, because the adapter validates only that the value is usable, never that it matches the root that pins it. cr-cwq therefore ships a contract ("the root pins one model per role and either the CLI runs that model or the activation fails") that this hole falsifies for any valid-but-wrong model.

Still pre-existing, so still not cr-cwq work: bdio/api.py is unchanged from 76771a8 and model=current.metadata.model predates the bead. But it is now the single largest gap between what the interpreter claims about its own evidence and what it enforces.

title: role bindings must pin model and effort, with a declared fallback model
description:
Nothing in the graph or the shipped config pins a model or a reasoning effort, so every live activation runs whatever the vendor CLI happens to default to.

Three layers all defer: the graph node names a role (runner = "profile:implementer"); the graph model field is the MODEL_VENDOR_DEFAULT sentinel "default", which means omit the flag (profiles/config.py:36-41); and config/foreman.example.toml:56-72 binds each role to a vendor only, with no model and no effort. ProfileConfig.effort is a per-vendor map (profiles/config.py:110-113) that the example config never sets, so effort_for returns None and no --effort / model_reasoning_effort is passed either.

Two consequences. A run is not reproducible: the same root re-instantiated after the vendor rolls its default silently executes on a different model. And a per-vendor effort map cannot express two claude roles at different efforts, which is the normal case (writer high, critic medium).

Owner ruling 2026-09-07: every role pins BOTH model and effort, plus a backup binding used when the pinned model is unavailable.

## Scope

1. RunnerBinding (foreman/config.py:14-21) requires model and effort; the MODEL_VENDOR_DEFAULT sentinel is refused for a role-bound node.
2. Effort becomes per-ROLE, resolved and pinned like model: new NodeSetting.EFFORT, carried on ResolvedNode, added to TaskSpec (supervisor/profile.py:126), read by claude.py:222 / codex.py:317 / opencode from the spec instead of ProfileConfig.effort_for.
3. A fallback binding per role, with the detection mechanism decided separately.
4. config/foreman.example.toml documents the pinned set.

## Acceptance criteria

A role binding without a model or an effort fails config load with a message naming the role; a bound node dispatches with explicit --model and --effort flags asserted in a proc-marked test; two claude roles at different efforts are expressible and both reach their CLI; the pinned pair is readable off the immutable root as evidence after the run.
notes:
OWNER DECISION 2026-09-07: option A (probe at instantiate) chosen over dispatch-time retry and validate-only.

MEASURED on this host during briefing, which splits option A into two mechanisms:
- claude --help declares a NATIVE --fallback-model <model>: "automatic fallback to specified model(s) when the default model is overloaded or not available. Accepts a comma-separated list to try each in order. Re-tries the primary at the start of each user turn. (only works with --print)". The claude profile already invokes with -p (profiles/claude.py:51,185,199), so this is available for free. No probe needed for claude, and nothing diverges from the pinned root because the primary is still what was asked for.
- codex --help declares no equivalent. Nor does opencode. Those two need the instantiate-time probe, pinning the fallback with a new ConfigSource.ROLE_BINDING_FALLBACK so the root records the substitution.

The probe command itself is NOT hardcoded: I could not verify a cheap model-existence check for codex, so the probe is injected per-vendor config shaped like binary_overrides, which also makes it testable against the existing stub executables. No configured probe means the primary is pinned unprobed.

Accepted consequence: a fallback substitution changes the resolved config, so create_root byte-exact reuse (bdio/roots.py:268-272) refuses a later re-instantiate. That refusal is correct and its message must name the substitution.

title: ADR 0003: probe the REAL bd metadata ceiling on the production path
description: Phase-0 probe 2 used --metadata=@file.json (scratchpad/probes/phase0-results.md:19-23). Production passes canonical JSON inline as ONE argv element (bdio/client.py:334-335). Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 32 x 4096 = 131072 bytes. So the probe validated a path production never takes and the real ceiling is likely ~128KiB, kernel-imposed. (1) Sweep/binary-search serialized sizes around failure using a real RootMetadata; multibyte UTF-8; create, self-ID merge, list/show, restart, same-key recreation; record exact failure sizes, failure modes, latency. (2) Test whether --metadata=@file is faithful on create with read-back: if so, switching BdClient lifts the ceiling and may remove the need for git-backed bodies entirely. Hazard: @file is broken for --event-payload, storing the literal '@file' and exiting 0 (client.py:337-338); _assert_metadata (client.py:404) read-back-verifies metadata so a break would be loud. Gates ADR 0002 size caps and the ADR 0003 storage mechanism. Does NOT gate ADR 0002 itself.
close_reason: Probe run 2026-09-03 against an isolated /tmp bd workspace. Inline argv (production path): largest payload created AND read-back-verified = 130818 chars; fails at 131329 with OSError Errno 7 'Argument list too long' — the kernel MAX_ARG_STRLEN (32*4096=131072), hit before bd runs. Failure mode is loud, never silent truncation. --metadata @file on create: verified exact at 70KB/200KB/1MB/4MB. --metadata @file on update (root self-ID merge): verified exact at 300KB with sibling keys preserved. Multibyte UTF-8: limit is bytes not chars (60000B ok, 120000B fails). CONCLUSION: phase-0 probe 2 measured a path production never takes; the ceiling is the kernel's, not bd's; switching BdClient to @file lifts it >=30x on both create and merge. Git-object bodies are NOT needed. Recorded in docs/adr/0003.

title: phase-5 LIVE finding: a no-progress gate offers 'approve', which its target node cannot route — the instance stalls permanently
description:
Found by the DRILL-27 live acceptance run (cr-o85.32), instance beads-f3e.
Reproduced deterministically: every subsequent tick returns the same stall.

WHAT HAPPENED. The forced first rejection worked (see cr-o85.32 notes), so the
rework had nothing real to fix and produced a byte-IDENTICAL artifact tree
(68c17b3f for both implement r1 beads-2ua and implement r2 beads-4dg). The §5
NO_PROGRESS breaker fired correctly and opened a human gate at `triage`
(beads-ayz, gate_reason=transition, opening_outcome=done).

`foreman status` named the inbox and rendered the template (the cr-tl3 fix).
A real ssh-keygen ed25519 signature over the canonical payload verified and the
gate closed cleanly: closed_gates=["beads-ayz"]. §9 works end to end.

Then the instance STALLED, permanently:
  {"stalled":"gate route is not a task", ...}   # every tick, forever

ROOT CAUSE. `foreman/gates.py::no_progress_gate` hardcodes
`outcomes=(Outcome.APPROVE, Outcome.ABANDON)` and ignores the target node's own
declared outcomes. Its target here is `triage`, which the shipped
feature-delivery graph declares as
    outcomes = ["rebudget", "abandon"]
with edges `triage --rebudget--> implement` and `triage --abandon--> abandoned`.
So `approve` has NO declared edge from `triage`. Routing falls through to the
graph fallback `[fallback] to = "triage"`, whose target is a GATE node, not a
task — and `foreman/cases.py:393` stalls with "gate route is not a task".

Contrast `exhaustion_gate` immediately above it, which offers
(APPROVE, REBUDGET, ABANDON) — also not the node's declared set, but at least
containing a routable member.

WHY IT MATTERS. The system offered a human an outcome it cannot act on, then
consumed a valid signed approval for it and dead-ended. There is no recovery:
the gate is closed, the outcome is recorded, and every tick re-stalls. A human
who picks the FIRST listed outcome bricks the instance.

FIX DIRECTION (not chosen): derive a gate's offered outcomes from the target
node's declared `outcomes` — as `transition_gate` already does
(`outcomes=node.outcomes or ()`, gates.py:79) — rather than hardcoding a
vocabulary per gate kind. If a breaker genuinely needs a verb the node does not
declare, the validator should refuse the graph at load time instead of letting
the mismatch appear at run time.

Cross-check worth doing: `exhaustion_gate`'s hardcoded APPROVE has the same
shape of problem wherever `on_exhausted` names a node that does not declare it.
close_reason: FIXED and proven live. exhaustion_gate and no_progress_gate now take their outcomes from the TARGET NODE (foreman/gates.py), exactly as transition_gate already did, instead of a vocabulary hardcoded per gate kind. Test: tests/test_foreman_functional.py::test_a_breaker_gate_only_offers_outcomes_its_own_node_can_route asserts the real invariant — every verb a gate offers must route TASK or TERMINAL — over both breaker gates; written RED first and it reproduced the live stall exactly ('triage offers approve, which routes fallback'). The fix exposed a second latent bug: payload_template took outcomes[0] blindly, which was only safe while every gate led with approve; with triage leading with rebudget the rendered template violated §9 (bound_mutation legal IFF outcome is rebudget) and so was no longer signable, breaking the template's own contract. Fixed by skipping rebudget when another verb exists. Proven live on beads-bmr: the ship gate offered ['approve','abandon'], both routable, and approve reached terminal. NOTED: drill 23's own test asserts these gates' region, round and key and never their outcomes — which is why the lab stayed green.

title: phase-5 LIVE finding: nothing tells a real runner the §6 channel protocol — the composed brief is inputs only
description:
Found by the DRILL-27 live acceptance run (cr-o85.32), first attempt, and NOT
findable in the lab: the ShellProfile double always wrote its outcome marker
because the test authored the script that wrote it. A real vendor CLI has no
idea the channel exists.

WHAT HAPPENED. Live instance beads-75j, node `implement`, runner claude-opus-5,
real repo, real bd. The runner did the work correctly — it wrote src/slug.py
and tests/test_slug.py, and `scripts/verify-feature.sh` passed (exit_code 0 in
the recorded evidence). It then exited 0 having:
  - never written $WF_OUTCOME_FILE,
  - never written $WF_EFFECTS_FILE,
  - never committed (the files are still untracked in the worktree).
Outcome graded `fail_code`; halt gate beads-cot opened with
halt_reason=fail_code:implement:beads-cke. evidence.outputs_tree_oid is the
EMPTY tree 4b825dc6.

ROOT CAUSE. The channels are exported into the child env correctly
(supervisor/profile.py:118-131 — ENV_OUTCOME_FILE, ENV_ARTIFACT_DIR,
ENV_EFFECTS_FILE, plus the §7.4 committer identity). What does not exist is any
place that TELLS the runner to use them. foreman/inputs.py::DefaultComposer
composes the brief as `"\n".join(item.text for item in inputs)` plus the
optional FORCED_FIRST_REJECT clause and nothing else, so the argv the profile
builds is `claude -p <the task brief verbatim>`. Nothing in
profiles/claude.py adds a system prompt or preamble. Spec §6:612-619 defines
the three channels and their fail-closed semantics but never assigns the duty
of communicating them.

CONSEQUENCE. As shipped, a real runner cannot reach `done` on a writing node
except by accident. Every live node fails closed. This is a v1 blocker for
§13's "one real small feature, Claude as first foreman".

WHAT WORKED, and it is worth recording: the foreman's fail-closed path is
exactly right. No marker -> fail_code, not a guessed success; the halt gate
opened with a precise halt_reason; `foreman status` surfaced the gate with its
inbox and payload template (the cr-tl3 fix, live).

FIX OPTIONS, not yet chosen:
  a. A runner-protocol preamble owned by the composer (one place, every node,
     derived from the node's own writes/allowed_paths/outcomes so it cannot
     drift from the graph).
  b. A per-profile system-prompt carrying the same, so each vendor phrases it
     in its own idiom.
  c. Declare it the brief author's job and document it — rejected on its face:
     it makes every brief carry harness protocol, and a brief that forgets it
     fails closed with no diagnostic pointing at the omission.

Option (a) is the natural home: the composer already owns brief composition and
already reads the node.
close_reason: FIXED and proven live. foreman/inputs.py::DefaultComposer now prepends the §6 channel contract, rendered per node from its OWN permissions and declared outcomes (constants.py RUNNER_PROTOCOL + the write/no-write step). implement gets 'git add and git commit ... <one of: done, no_diff, fail_plan>'; review gets 'Do NOT write to the repository ... <one of: accept, reject>'. Test: tests/test_foreman_inputs.py::test_compose_tells_the_runner_the_channel_protocol_for_its_own_node, parametrized over both nodes, written RED first. Proven live on instance beads-bmr with the manual preamble REMOVED from brief.md, so the product path is what ran: all four activations wrote both channels and the writing ones committed.

title: phase-5: infra-retry after ANY gate-origin re-mint crashes the tick and strands the instance
description: foreman/cases.py:409-414 builds the INFRA_RETRY mint request via _request() and model_copy(update={'mint_reason', 'predecessor_activation_id'}) — it never clears predecessor_gate_id, which _request() copies verbatim from the closed activation at cases.py:121. Any activation minted from a gate decision (halt approve/rebudget, exhaustion rebudget) carries predecessor_gate_id. When such an activation later closes error_runner, the auto infra-retry request therefore carries BOTH predecessor_activation_id and predecessor_gate_id, and bdio/mint.py:238-244 _assert_reason_matches refuses it: a request with predecessor_gate_id must have mint_reason EDGE. CarrierIntegrityError is caught NOWHERE in workflow_interpreter/foreman/ (cases.py:432 catches only BoundExceededError), so it propagates unhandled out of tick(). The activation stays closed error_runner, so EVERY subsequent tick re-enters the same path: a permanent crash loop with no halt gate, no stalled report, and no human escape at the foreman seam. Secondary: the diagnostic at mint.py:244 is misleading — it interpolates the GATE id with the ACTIVATION predecessor's outcome ('requires its predecessor to have closed edge, but wf-12 closed error_runner').
design: Likely one line: the model_copy(update=...) at cases.py:409 must also set predecessor_gate_id=None. An infra retry re-attempts the same logical activation; its causal predecessor is that activation, not the gate that originally minted it. Needs a ruling on whether gate provenance should instead be preserved by relaxing the mint.py guard — but the guard's stated rationale ('a mislabeled mint would be counted against the wrong 10.2 bound') argues for clearing the field, not relaxing the guard. Confirm no other model_copy over a _request() has the same gap.
acceptance_criteria: A drill-level test drives: dirty-tree refusal -> halt -> approve -> gate-origin re-mint runs -> that activation closes error_runner -> the next tick MINTS an infra retry (no exception), and the node still gets its FULL max_infra_retries because the precondition-refused closes did not count (P14, bdio/bounds.py:360-364). tests/test_foreman_functional.py::test_drill_26_a_real_infra_failure_after_the_dirty_tree_recovery_keeps_the_full_budget is that test and is RED today.
notes: 2026-09-01 FIXED. foreman/cases.py:409 now builds a fresh MintRequest field by field (omitting predecessor_gate_id) instead of _request(...).model_copy(update=...), so _validate_predecessors runs and the carrier invariant is ENFORCED at construction rather than relied upon — Sol's preferred shape over the minimal one-line None. Evidence: the drill-26 P14 test went RED->GREEN with no test edit; mutant B2-M7 (revert the fix) is KILLED by that test, so the fix is load-bearing; mutant B2-M1 (drop the PRECONDITION_REFUSED skip at bdio/bounds.py:360-364) is KILLED by that test, so P14 is now PROVEN — it was unprovable while this defect stood. Gate: 971 passed / 23 deselected, ruff+format+mypy clean. One product file changed (+20/-10).

title: Assess cross-runtime Agent Matrix skill
description: Determine whether one reusable skill can select role prompts, models, effort, capabilities, and invocation policy and then spawn Claude Code and Codex subagents without a Cartesian catalog of agent definitions. Separate what a skill can decide from what each runtime can enforce.
design: Recommend Agent Matrix as the source-of-truth catalog and orchestration workflow, with role prompts and defaults in skill references plus a deterministic resolver. Do not treat the skill as a security/configuration boundary. Codex V2 can dynamically select role, model, reasoning effort, and fork policy, but not arbitrary per-spawn capabilities/permissions. Claude skills can run in forked subagent context and have static model/effort/agent frontmatter; arbitrary per-request combinations require an inline orchestrator plus limited Agent overrides, a small set of capability archetype agents, or a pre-session launcher that emits session-scoped --agents JSON. Preserve role instructions in real agent definitions whenever system/developer-prompt authority is required.
acceptance_criteria: Answer gives a clear yes/no boundary for both runtimes, identifies metadata that can and cannot be set per spawn, recommends a practical architecture, and distinguishes orchestration guidance from enforced subagent configuration.
close_reason: Completed the source-grounded feasibility assessment: one Agent Matrix skill can own selection and prompt cataloging, but cannot dynamically enforce every agent field on both runtimes. Recorded the recommended hybrid architecture and the Claude/Codex per-spawn boundaries.

title: Migration peek opens and writes SQLite before taking the ledger fence
description:
Found in the cr-3411 final epic review (Sol 5.6 high finding 2 BLOCKER; Fable examined the same area and reported no findings — Sol is right on the facts). Verified in code.

ledger/database.py:_migrate_if_behind peeks at the schema version with connect(self._path) before acquiring any fence. Its docstring calls this 'an unfenced read', but connect() with read_only=False does path.parent.mkdir(...), creates the database file if absent, and executes the full PRAGMAS list (including foreign_keys=ON and the journal-mode setting). That is a create-and-write, not a read.

§3.4 requires every connection to hold the shared fence and migration to hold it exclusively. While an import, restore or another migration holds the exclusive fence, a starting process can still create the file and negotiate journal mode.

Severity: MAJOR rather than BLOCKER — harm needs a concurrent restore. Likely fix is one argument (read_only=True) plus a test, since the peek only ever reads a version.

Cheap and orthogonal to the store redesign.
acceptance_criteria: The pre-fence peek cannot create the database file or execute a write pragma; a test asserts a peek against a missing ledger does not create it.

Residual limitation recorded in the bead's notes. cr-hf85: the pre-fence peek opens read-only and treats LedgerAbsent as 'behind, go migrate' (04a249f, test 2c4f50e). Canonical gate on merged main: 2 failed, 2265 passed; both failures are cr-k88e.1 flakes that also failed at baseline and pass in isolation.

title: verify_export does not bind signature rows to the task's own gates
description:
Found in the cr-3411 final epic review (Sol 5.6 high finding 1 BLOCKER, Fable 5.1 high finding 4 MINOR; verified in code).

ledger/reverify.py:524-562 asks three questions: are the signatures valid over these bytes, are these the bytes git pinned for this task, and is the signer trusted. It never compares a signature row's payload root_id, gate_key, nonce or outcome against the export's own gates and nonces rows.

So a fresh clone proves 'a trusted key signed these bytes', not 'these bytes are the approvals recorded on this task's gates'. Task B's valid export placed at task A's committed export path would pass all four answers as A's approvals.

Severity judgement: Sol called this a BLOCKER, Fable a MINOR. Fable's counter-argument holds — the trust anchor is the committed blob in HEAD, so anyone who can place B's bytes at A's export path can commit anything. Not exploitable under that residual trust, but D21 claims more than the code proves.

Cheap and orthogonal to the store redesign: cross-check inside the export that is already being read.
acceptance_criteria: verify_export refuses, or reports unverified, any signature row whose payload does not name a gate belonging to the task being verified; a test transplants another task's signature row and asserts the refusal.
notes:
Fixed on wf/run-ledger in d25667a. Orchestrator review of the diff found a RESIDUAL gap worth recording rather than re-opening:

The binding is checked against the export's OWN gates/nonces rows. That defeats the two realistic cases — a foreign signature row transplanted into an honest export, and a whole foreign export left at this task's path (its gates rows carry the other task_id) — both of which now have tests.

It does NOT defeat a fully crafted export. An author of arbitrary export bytes can write a gates row claiming task_id=A while setting root_id/gate_key to the values inside a payload signed for task B, and the binding passes. Nothing cross-checks that gate.root_id belongs to task_id (ledger root ids have the form <task>-a<n>, so the inconsistency is detectable but undetected).

Acceptable under the residual trust of HEAD — anyone who can commit arbitrary bytes at A's export path can commit anything — which is the same argument that made this a MINOR for Fable. Recorded so the store redesign can decide whether re-verification should also check id-to-task consistency. Related: cr-vmgq item 2 notes that ledger root id derivation already drifts from the pinned attempt, so that check would need the id form to be trustworthy first.
close_reason: Fixed on wf/run-ledger and merged to main in e3ad26e. cr-f8lu: verify_export now binds each approval to a gates row this export carries for this task (d25667a), with RED->GREEN tests that reproduced the defect first — the whole-foreign-export case was fully accepted at baseline. Residual limitation recorded in the bead's notes. cr-hf85: the pre-fence peek opens read-only and treats LedgerAbsent as 'behind, go migrate' (04a249f, test 2c4f50e). Canonical gate on merged main: 2 failed, 2265 passed; both failures are cr-k88e.1 flakes that also failed at baseline and pass in isolation.

title: Settle the three budgets: envelope bytes, dead token_budget, runner context window
description:
Three budget knobs exist and only one does anything. Decide what each is for, then make the graph say it.

1. token_budget (node field, set on every feature-delivery task: 120000/40000/80000) is IGNORED. foreman/inputs.py:471 emits the diagnostic legacy_token_budget_ignored and nothing else reads it. Either map it to a real budget or fail graph validation on it — silent dead config is the worst of the three options.

2. context_budget_bytes is the only enforced budget. foreman/inputs.py:465 passes it to compose_envelope as 'limit', defaulting to 262144 bytes tagged legacy_safety_default when unset. compose_envelope (foreman/envelope.py:64-110) counts the FULL framed text and drops optional sections in trim_priority order until it fits, recording each drop in an omissions manifest with a sha256; if only mandatory sections remain and it still does not fit it raises EnvelopeRefusal, which surfaces as the input_oversize decision trigger. No feature-delivery node sets it, so all three run on the legacy default. Question to settle: is a byte cap on injected material still the right instrument, and should it be pinned per node instead of inherited from a default nobody chose?

3. The runner's own context window is not configured at all. The engine passes no context/window/max-tokens flag to claude or codex; each CLI uses its vendor default. This is the actual gap: the engine trims what it injects without knowing what the model can hold.

The three are unrelated units (engine-injected bytes vs model tokens vs vendor window) and are currently confusable by name alone.
acceptance_criteria: 1. token_budget is either wired to a real budget or rejected by the validator, with no silent-ignore path left. 2. The envelope byte budget's purpose and default are decided and documented, and every feature-delivery node states its own value if the default is not deliberate. 3. A node or execution profile can declare the runner context window and the wrapper passes it to the runner CLI.
notes: Raised 2026-09-18 while walking the graph schema. Related dead config: every feature-delivery task node sets token_budget (120000/40000/80000) and none sets context_budget_bytes, so all three run on the 256 KiB legacy default.

title: Seed the shared toolchain cache on the host before dispatch (offline sandbox cannot fetch interpreters or wheels)
description:
Observed on DWS root cr-xozb round 1 (activation cr-i0kn) right after cr-02ze.18 landed: the Codex writer could now write the wrapper-wide uv cache, but the cache was empty and the sandbox is network-denied, so uv run tried to download cpython-3.13.9 (the dws lock) and failed on DNS. The implementer reported fail_plan honestly. Coordinator worked around it by hand on the host: copied the uv-managed cpython-3.13.9 into <wrapper_root>/uv-cache/python (the UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR the launcher exports, supervisor/launch.py) and ran uv sync --locked for the target project with UV_CACHE_DIR pointed at the wrapper cache; then UV_OFFLINE=1 uv run --frozen ruff resolved. Round 2 then passed the host gate.

Gap: nothing in the engine seeds the cache. toolchain_cache_for (supervisor/sandbox.py) creates an empty directory; every fresh wrapper root starts cold and offline, so any uv-based local check in a brief is unsatisfiable until a human warms the cache. This is the second half of cr-02ze.18.

Proposal: a host-side, pre-dispatch warm step owned by the supervisor or foreman (never by the sandboxed node): for the instance repo_root, run uv python install <locked version> with UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=<cache>/python and uv sync --locked (or --frozen) with UV_CACHE_DIR=<cache> for the project directories the graph declares (repo root and any allowed_paths subproject with a uv.lock), before the first activation is minted; record what was seeded in the launch receipt; make the warm step idempotent and skip when the cache already resolves offline. Do not give the sandbox network. Also document the manual recipe in docs/usage until the automation lands.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh wrapper root for a project with a uv.lock lets a codex writer activation run UV_OFFLINE=1 uv run --frozen ruff --version successfully on its first round without any manual host warming; the launch receipt records the seeded interpreter and lock digest; a test covers the cold-cache path with a stub uv.
notes: Design ruling 2026-09-15 (user): never re-download. Seed the per-run cache from the host uv cache (~/.cache/uv, or `uv cache dir`) and the host uv-managed interpreter dir by a real copy (cp --reflink=auto; falls back to a plain copy on filesystems without reflink, e.g. WSL ext4). Do NOT share, symlink, or hardlink the host cache into the sandbox: the writer node can write its cache, and a shared inode would let an agent poison packages for every later uv run on the host (the cross-node write channel the .18 reviewer flagged). Only fall back to a network fetch on the host when the host cache lacks something the lock needs. Expected cost: seconds, not minutes.

title: Feed the failed verify output into the implement rework activation
description:
Graphs declare implement --fail_code--> implement (the DWS graph comments it as: a red check is a rework, not a human halt). But the rework activation receives only the declared inputs, e.g. inputs = [task_brief, review_findings]; the verify failure that caused the fail_code is not among them. foreman/tick.py _verify_inspections (around line 188) feeds red tails only into the read-only inspect/status report, never into the next envelope. So the implementer is sent back with no evidence of what failed and, on DWS root cr-9av3, reproduced a byte-identical candidate in round 2.

Observed: activation cr-6zhw fail_code -> rebudget -> activation cr-ha8x fail_code, same file, same hunk, same claimed done. The review_findings input was omitted as missing on both rounds because review never ran.

Proposal: add a declared, optional, trim-prioritized source (e.g. verify_findings, producer node:implement or producer instance) carrying the bounded red tails of the previous same-node activation on a fail_code edge, subject to the existing context_budget_bytes. Keep it a fact for the model, not an instruction; do not let it bypass the host gate. This is separate from cr-02ze.NEW-sandbox-bug: even with feedback, a Codex implementer still cannot run uv today, so land that first.
acceptance_criteria: On an implement fail_code -> implement edge, the new activation envelope includes the previous activation red tails under a declared source name, bounded by context_budget_bytes, and the status output lists it under included; a foreman test covers the two-round case; no change to grading or gate logic.
notes: The placeholder cr-02ze.NEW-sandbox-bug in the description means cr-02ze.18. Land .18 first: without a writable uv cache the implementer cannot act on the feedback anyway.

Preserve local/host verification contract and TDD red evidence. Avoid copying writer-irrelevant clauses. Keep extra reviewer instruction bytes small (aim <=900 UTF8 perreview node, explain if more needed). Add focused characterization/regression tests for authored/packaged equality, role outcome compatibility and preserved verification/routing; literal text checks are not mechanicalmodelproof. Test-first where needed. Engine runs scripts/verify-engine-bootstrap.sh after each node and fullhost gate before landing. Commit exactscoped candidate, emit normal outcome/effects/report. ## MAJOR 1 — the briefed documentation deliverable is absent, and this is a regression from round 1

Brief: "Document opt-in usage and limitations."

There is no documentation of `artifact_input_mode` anywhere in the tree. A
repository-wide grep for the field name matches only source, tests, the JSON
schema, and `docs/plans/pointer-handoff.md` — the *superseded* plan the brief
itself says it replaces. `docs/usage/` contains `phase-bridge.md`,
`mvp-plugin.md` and `children.md` and nothing else; `docs/specs/` does not
mention the mode at all. Round 1 shipped `docs/usage/pointer-handoff.md` (cited
at `:14-16` in the round-1 report); round 2's diff does not contain it and the
file does not exist, so the round-2 rewrite dropped it.

The only prose a graph author can find is the one-line schema description at
`workflow_interpreter/schema/graph_schema.json:209-213`, "How producer evidence
is delivered to this task. Omit for the legacy inline behavior."

Concrete failure: an author sets `artifact_input_mode = "references"` on a
`review` node in a graph whose instance runs with `sandbox = off`. Nothing
warns them; the dispatch dies at `launch.py:958-961` with
`_MSG_REFERENCE_REVIEW_NEEDS_BOUND`, after the engine has already exported the
evidence set to disk. The same author has no written statement of the other two
behaviour changes the mode carries — the loss of the optional-input omission
path (MINOR 2 below) and the export size ceilings at
`evidence_export.py:26-30` — so the first time either is discovered is as a
refused activation in a live root.

## MAJOR 2 — nothing proves the runner *permission layers* can follow the pointer; only the bubblewrap mount is proven

Brief: "prove Claude existing Read permission can access them, and Codex can
read them; actual production sandbox file reads succeed and writes to
exports/source/engine records fail."

The second half is now proven:
`tests/test_supervisor_sandbox.py:706-740` reads the index through a real
`bwrap` box and asserts refusals on the export, the checkout and
`launch-receipt.json`. The first half is not proven by anything. No test in
this diff touches `workflow_interpreter/profiles/claude.py` or
`workflow_interpreter/profiles/codex.py`, and `tests/test_profiles_command.py`
— which *is* in `scripts/verify-pointer-handoff.sh:4` — was not extended.

This is a real, layered gap, not a duplicate of the bwrap probe. Claude's own
module docstring says it is "bounded by permission rules, not a sandbox"
(`workflow_interpreter/profiles/claude.py:183`); the property reference mode
depends on is that `READ_TOOLS` at `claude.py:65` is the *unscoped* `("Read",
"Glob", "Grep")` triple, with no path argument. For Codex the property is that
`workspace-write` (`codex.py:127-137`, `_sandbox_flags` at `:302-330`) bounds
*writes* only, while `_workspace_root` at `:274-300` roots a `writes = false`
node at `channels/` — one level *below* the activation directory the exports now
live in (`evidence_export.py:174`).

Concrete failure: a later hardening pass narrows `claude.py:65` to
`Read(<cwd>/**)` — exactly the shape `docs/plans/allowed-paths-enforcement.md`
is already pushing the profiles toward. Every verifier-covered test still
passes green, and every reference-mode reviewer from then on receives a pointer
to a path its own tool layer refuses to open: the review proceeds on the brief
alone, silently blind to the diff it was minted to read. The same holds if
Codex's writable-root grant is ever mistaken for a read grant and narrowed with
it.

## MINOR 1 — the symlink refusal is proven only against a mocked tree; the gitlink refusal is not proven at all

`tests/test_pointer_handoff.py:281-283` monkeypatches `git.tree_blobs` to return
a synthetic `("120000", "0"*40, "link")` tuple. That does exercise the
`_REGULAR_MODES` guard at `evidence_export.py:31, 148-149`, so a typo in the
mode set would be caught — but it never puts a real symlink blob in a real tree,
so it cannot catch a change in how `gitio.tree_blobs` parses `ls-tree` output.
The gitlink path is untested outright: `gitio.py:327-328` raises
`GitCommandError("report tree contains a non-blob entry")` for a `160000`
submodule entry, and nothing reaches it. Brief: "Accept only regular report
blobs; reject unsupported symlinks/gitlinks rather than following them."

## MINOR 2 — reference mode still drops the optional-input degradation path (round-1 MINOR 4, unchanged)

`workflow_interpreter/foreman/supervise.py:162-181` returns before
`bounded_materialize`, so the `GitOutputTooLarge` → `InputOmission` conversion at
`workflow_interpreter/foreman/inputs.py:284-301` is unreachable in reference
mode; `evidence_export.py:92-95` makes the same overflow fatal. A node with an
optional, non-essential input whose producer diff exceeds
`EXPORT_MAX_DIFF_BYTES` refuses the whole activation where the identical graph in
inline mode would run with a recorded omission. The brief does authorise "clear
refusal on overflow", so this may be intended — it is the *undocumented* part
that still stands, and MAJOR 1 is where it should have been written down.

## MINOR 3 — the sandbox-off refusal still fires after the export has been written (round-1 MINOR 5, unchanged)

`launch.py:884` calls `_sandbox` one line after `build_task` at `:883` has
already run `export_reference` and published a complete evidence directory.
Nothing launches, so the guarantee holds, but a `sandbox = off` instance pays
the full export — up to `EXPORT_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES` of writes — for a
configuration that can never be dispatched, and leaves the tree behind.

## MINOR 4 — a crash during `_publish` leaks a `.stage` directory nothing reclaims

`evidence_export.py:218-219` creates `.<name>.<uuid>.stage` under
`<activation>/evidence/`, and the cleanup at `:255-261` only runs when the
exception passes through the `except BaseException`. A SIGKILL between
`stage.mkdir` and `os.replace` leaves the partial directory in place forever:
the fingerprinted destination name at `:191` is unaffected, so the next export
republishes correctly, but the stale staging tree accumulates one entry per
crash with no sweep.

## MINOR 5 — the entry-count overflow reports itself as a byte overflow

`gitio.py:331` raises `GitOutputTooLarge(max_entries)`, whose message is
`f"git output exceeds {limit} bytes"` (`gitcmd.py:169-171`). A report tree with
257 entries therefore refuses with "git output exceeds 256 bytes", which
`evidence_export.py:93-95` forwards verbatim. The refusal is correct and the
operator reading it is pointed at the wrong limit.

## MINOR 6 — the output-snapshot producer path is never exercised

Every test builds a writer producer via `_pinned_writer`
(`tests/test_pointer_handoff.py:61-94`, node `implement`, `writes = true`), so
the non-writer branch at `evidence_export.py:85-91` — the binding check against
`outputs_ref`/`outputs_tree_oid` and `_reports(..., required=True)` at `:125-141`
— is unreached. Brief: "For output snapshots prove claimed outputs ref resolves
to the declared output tree."

## MINOR 7 — a non-UTF-8 report path fails closed, untested and unstated

`gitio.py:329` decodes logical paths with `surrogateescape`. A report blob whose
name carries invalid UTF-8 therefore reaches `json.dumps(...).encode()` at
`evidence_export.py:190` and `:251` carrying lone surrogates, raising
`UnicodeEncodeError`. That is caught and converted to `InputsUnavailable` at
`:106-109`, so it fails closed — correct, but it means "preserve unusual logical
paths as JSON data" has a silent exception, and `:326-370` tests only the
UTF-8-safe shell-metacharacter case.

title: Implement opt-in pointer handoffs with the original task contract
description:

This fully supersedes docs/plans/pointer-handoff.md and earlier direct-Git/no-export briefs where they conflict. User approved this simpler design after attempt2 was abandoned. Stage: cr-wi82.1. Start from the current clean workflow candidate base 197c8a2fcdd814a529233571ada88d225f1a1335. Do not cherry-pick failed candidates wholesale. You may inspect 07457c7d43f47a50b261a461967c00403f287ccf for reusable schema/validation ideas. Do not import its shell permission changes or 0b31d5c's network/cache changes.

Outcome: add opt-in graph task-node artifact_input_mode (inline | references; absent/None retains legacy inline and exact canonical hashes). Reference mode keeps the ORIGINAL instance task brief and role instructions inline. Only bound producer evidence becomes compact file pointers, never injected diff/report contents. This is graph-authored semantics, not a new CLI/project override. Reject invalid values or use on non-task nodes. Keep shipped graph defaults unchanged.

Export contract: trusted engine materializes complete diff text and report blobs from verified immutable Git evidence into a per-consumer activation directory under WrapperPaths.activation_dir, OUTSIDE channels and worktree, covered by the existing wrapper-root read-only mount. Pointer text gives a small index-file path and immutable provenance (producer id and relevant base/candidate/tree OIDs). Index contains diff-file path plus report entries with original logical path, blob OID and exported file path. Index/file counts stay out of the prompt. Use existing Read tool to inspect index, diff, and chosen reports; instructions require inspecting evidence and citing file/line findings. No new model tools, Bash grants, network isolation or cache policy changes. Do not add a new result JSON protocol; the small engine-owned file index is input evidence, distinct from model output. Do not change existing outcomes/effects files.

Before export: preserve existing binding/producer/ref/digest checks. For writers prove artifact ref resolves exactly candidate commit, its tree matches binding digest, and base is an existing ancestor commit. For output snapshots prove claimed outputs ref resolves to the declared output tree. Reject missing/moved/mismatched pins; if writer claims output evidence, validate it rather than silently omitting broken reports. Writers without any published report evidence may omit reports. Export from pinned Git blobs, never mutable live producer channels. Inline consumers must retain their existing validation/materialization behavior, without new reference-only checks.

Safe publication: engine-chosen numbered/hashed filenames, never use untrusted report path as a filesystem export destination. Preserve unusual logical paths as JSON data, never shell code. Accept only regular report blobs; reject unsupported symlinks/gitlinks rather than following them. Use existing safe durable-write conventions and reject symlink/collision escapes in export parents. Publish a complete evidence set and index atomically, or equivalent staging with index published last and no runner launch until complete. Repeat task construction/resume must validate/rebuild safely from pinned evidence, not trust stale partial files. File contents are allowed to be materialized on disk (old prohibition explicitly removed); use existing bounded Git execution and sensible finite export size/count limits with clear refusal on overflow, never silent truncation. Avoid a new storage service/database. Models cannot write exported evidence through production sandbox grants; sandbox-off reference mode must refuse rather than make a false read-only guarantee.

Ownership: workflow_interpreter/foreman, schema, narrowly needed supervisor/bdio, tests, docs/usage, docs/specs, config. No profile tool/permission changes, dependencies/lockfiles, workflow graphs/check scripts, root policies, Beads or reference repos. Other work exists: preserve it. Coordinator will not patch source inside this loop. Commit named allowed source paths in YOUR runtime worktree.

Test-first proof at real seams: >80KiB diff and report content represented by a final <=32768-byte envelope retaining complete original task brief; prompt contains paths and provenance but not bodies. Read exported files and compare to pinned Git diff/blobs even after producer live files change/disappear. Missing/moved/mismatched evidence fails closed. Legacy inline results and canonical fixture hashes unchanged. Wire actual task builder to protected export paths, prove Claude existing Read permission can access them, and Codex can read them; actual production sandbox file reads succeed and writes to exports/source/engine records fail. Do not claim sibling paths globally read-only: existing outer sandbox only protects its named roots. Cover unsupported sandbox-off refusal, malicious/unusual logical paths, partial publication/rebuild and oversized export refusal. Keep tests in existing verifier-covered files or tests/test_pointer_handoff.py, no paid live model calls. Document opt-in usage and limitations.

Verification: exact scripts/verify-pointer-handoff.sh is HOST ONLY after model exit (contains nested_sandbox probes). Locally run focused pytest with -m "not live and not nested_sandbox", Ruff check/format and strict mypy on workflow_interpreter. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1; unset UV_FROZEN for synthetic-project tests; MYPYPATH=. for mypy --strict --explicit-package-bases workflow_interpreter/. Temporary repos/caches go in WF_SCRATCH_DIR, NEVER WF_ARTIFACT_DIR. Do not repeat host-only nested tests or network/download failures inside sandbox. Report done only after source committed and supported local checks pass, explicitly noting host tests pending. Engine enforces full focused host verifier before advancing, full bridge gates before landing.

Write one concise report in WF_ARTIFACT_DIR: changes, red/green evidence, supported local checks, limitations. Use existing required outcome/effects protocol. Fail_plan for scope impossibility. Current running root remains pinned to old inline delivery; new file-pointer path is tested through focused integration tests and future roots, never by rewriting this run. Landing is isolated wf/pointer-handoff only, never main or DWS.

description: bdio/client.py:138-142 declares DependencyRecord with zero fields and extra=allow; list_dependencies validates every row into it. Slice 2 computes a blocked CLI state (plan lines 33-36, 268-270) and cannot do so from a fieldless passthrough without dict access that mypy --strict will not accept. Fix when Slice 2 needs it: run a real bd dep list --json, read the actual field names and types, and declare id, direction and status from what was observed - not from memory or docs.
close_reason: Landed in 275c874 (Slice 2a): prepare() refuses to overwrite a stored journal past PREPARED; DependencyRecord declares id/status/dependency_type over the full documented bd vocabulary with unknown values normalized to a non-blocking UNKNOWN, plus blocking_dependencies() excluding parent-child and closed rows.

title: Guard PhaseAdapter.prepare against clobbering a later-state journal
description: prepare() (bridge/adapter.py:171-176) asserts only the state of the record PASSED IN, never the stored one. A fresh next_attempt() record therefore overwrites any existing journal regardless of how far that stage had progressed. Confirmed during the Slice 1 blind review (Sol finding 3, adjudicated PARTIAL/slice-1). Fix: read the stored record and refuse to overwrite any state past PREPARED.
close_reason: Landed in 275c874 (Slice 2a): prepare() refuses to overwrite a stored journal past PREPARED; DependencyRecord declares id/status/dependency_type over the full documented bd vocabulary with unknown values normalized to a non-blocking UNKNOWN, plus blocking_dependencies() excluding parent-child and closed rows.

title: A merge-resolution graph: a parked landing becomes ordinary reviewed work
description:
Owner proposal 2026-09-10, adopted. Instead of the orchestrator resolving a conflict inline, it files a bead and dispatches a dedicated merge-resolution graph. The artifact that graph produces IS the merge commit.

WHY THIS IS BETTER than inline resolution: an inline resolution is content nobody reviewed, which forced a new special-case rule - "an authored resolution needs its own signature". Routing it through a graph deletes that rule. The resolution gets implement, review and a normal ship gate like any other work, and because the merge commit already contains both parents, landing it is a pure fast-forward with nothing further to merge or verify.

TECHNICALLY FREE, verified 2026-09-10: supervisor/artifact.py:90 pin_artifact reads whatever HEAD the RUNNER produced and pins it - the wrapper does not create the commit. Its attribution test is descent: intended_base_commit must be an ANCESTOR of head. A merge commit M with parents H-prime and A, where H-prime is the intended base, passes. The declaration test does not apply, per artifact.py:117-118 "Worktree mode never applies it: the tree is the wrapper own and nobody else commits in it". So a merge commit is already a legal artifact; nobody designed for it, it falls out.

WHY ITS OWN GRAPH, not feature-delivery: the input is two OIDs and a conflict rather than a task brief; the review question is "does this preserve both intents" rather than "does this match the brief"; the bounds should be far tighter than 45m implement plus 3 rounds; and it needs an extra outcome - "cannot be resolved, the original work is invalidated" - which is the one case where re-running the stage is correct, expressed as a graph outcome instead of a policy.

UNVERIFIED, check before building: whether the runner can execute git merge inside its sandbox. The SUPERVISOR transport forbids merge (supervisor/gitcmd.py:99-102) but the runner is a separate agent with its own shell. Likely yes; not confirmed.

KNOWN RISK, measure rather than pre-solve: thrashing. If resolution takes ~10 min and stages arrive every ~3, HEAD may move again before the resolution lands. In practice the second merge is usually clean because the hard part is done. Bounded in practice, not in theory.
acceptance_criteria: A textual conflict or a clean merge with a red repo gate parks the landing and opens a resolution bead; the resolution graph produces a merge commit as its artifact; that artifact passes a normal ship gate and lands by fast-forward; an unresolvable conflict exits through a distinct graph outcome rather than a policy decision.

title: Landing: a serialized queue that merges, with parked collisions resolved through a graph
description:
Owner ruling 2026-09-10, superseding the fast-forward-only landing in bridge plan v9.

WHY the ff-only design was too narrow: it does not degrade under concurrency, it forbids it. Two graphs from the same base H produce A1 and A2 whose parent is H. A1 lands. A2 is then not a descendant of HEAD, so --ff-only refuses - always, with no race and no timing window. Within one phase this never bites (stage 2 is created after stage 1 lands, so its base is already A1); across concurrent phases or workstreams it bites every time.

RULING: land with an ordinary merge. Fast-forward when the branch has not moved, merge commit when it has.

THE PROBLEM THIS OPENS: a merge commit M has a different tree and a different OID than the signed artifact A. The ship gate binds immutable - bdio/gates.py refuses to close unless payload.artifact.commit_oid equals gate.metadata.artifact_ref. So the human signature binds A and does not bind M. Rebase has the same defect and is worse.

PROPOSED RULE (needs a ruling): split on whether a human authored content.
- Clean merge: M has exactly two parents, H and A, and its tree is reproducible by re-running the merge. Provenance is CHECKABLE, so no second signature. The receipt records M, its two parents, and that the merge was clean.
- Conflicted merge: a human authored content nobody approved. That needs its own signature, and only then.

This is narrower than v8, which demanded a signing ceremony for every landing.

CONSEQUENCE: pre-landing verification becomes MORE important, not less. M may be a tree no one has ever tested. The repo gate must run on M in a detached scratch worktree before the real branch moves. supervisor/verify.py:137 VerifyTree is close but not identical - it asserts head == commit on a plain checkout, and this needs a checkout of H that a merge is then performed in.

STAYS CUT from v8: the CAS, the band lock across admission and landing, the conflict fixture and interloper, the OID-bound resolution gate with its nine-field payload, and the blanket per-landing ceremony.
acceptance_criteria: A landing whose branch has not moved fast-forwards to the signed OID. A landing whose branch has moved produces a merge commit, verifies the repo gate on that merge commit in a detached tree before the branch moves, and records both parents in the receipt. A conflicted merge refuses and reports; it never auto-resolves. A ruling is recorded on what authorizes a merge commit the signature does not cover.
notes:
Owner rulings 2026-09-10, in conversation:

1. LAND BY MERGE, not ff-only. Fast-forward when the branch has not moved, merge commit when it has. ff-only does not degrade under concurrency, it FORBIDS it: two graphs from base H produce artifacts whose parent is H, the first lands, and every later one is not a descendant of HEAD so --ff-only always refuses.

2. SERIALIZE LANDING, NOT WORK. The graph run is the expensive part (36-55 min, $2-4) and stays parallel. The repo gate is cheap (measured ~4 min this session: 76s + 22s + 105s + 19s + checks) and serializes behind a landing lock. Ten stages: ~400 min fully serial, ~80 min with parallel graphs and a serial landing queue, ~50 min if clean merges are batched into one gate run.

3. PARKED, NOT ABANDONED. A stuck landing never blocks the queue and never discards the work. Re-running a stage is for work that is genuinely invalidated, NOT a collision policy - a policy of abandon-on-collision makes concurrency cost more than working serially, which is self-defeating.

4. THREE LANDING PATHS. (a) HEAD unmoved: fast-forward, repo gate on A, land. (b) HEAD moved, clean merge: repo gate on M - M is a tree nobody has tested. Green lands with NO new signature, because M has exactly two parents and its tree is reproducible by re-running the merge, so provenance is checkable. (c) HEAD moved, conflict OR clean-merge-with-red-gate: park and resolve through a graph. The red-gate case is the one a conflict check misses - B renames a function, A calls the old name, different files, git merges cleanly, code is broken.

5. VERIFY BEFORE THE BRANCH MOVES. Mandatory now rather than merely cheaper: M may be a tree neither the implementer, the reviewer, nor the signer ever saw.

STILL CUT from v8: the CAS (a landing lock makes compare-and-swap unnecessary - one writer), the band lock across admission AND landing (the lock is scoped to landing only), the conflict fixture and interloper commit, the OID-bound resolution gate with its nine-field payload, and the per-landing signing ceremony.

title: create_root validates the pinned body only AFTER writing it — move validation before _create_bead
description:
Discovered while fixing cr-xb2 round 6, by observing what the RED test actually printed.

create_root ALREADY enforces the graph schema. It does so too late. The post-write path _converged_root -> _ensure_self_id -> parse_root -> load_pinned_body re-validates the pinned body against graph_schema.json. Observed directly: a task node with runner="claude" logs wf.root.created root_id=wf-1 and THEN raises PinnedGraphMismatchError with "schema at $.node[0].runner: claude does not match ^profile:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$".

So a schema-invalid programmatic body is not silently accepted. It is WRITTEN, then rejected -- leaving the caller an exception plus a permanently poisoned instance key, because root identity refuses to recreate that key with a corrected body. The invariant exists; only its ordering is wrong.

FIX DIRECTION, and note it is NOT a ^profile: regex. Call load_pinned_body(canonical_bytes(definition.document), allow_test_flags=allow_test_flags) up beside the other _assert_ guards, before _create_bead. That makes create-time and load-time agree by construction and closes EVERY schema drift at once, not just runner -- any programmatic model_copy producing a body the reader will later refuse. A hand-written pattern check at this boundary would be a second narrower copy of a rule the schema already owns, and it would drift.

The boundary is correct: create_root is already the documented chokepoint for _assert_tasks_are_instructed, precisely because there is no CLI instantiate command and labs call it directly. The programmatic path is the one the TOML loader never covers.

WHAT IT BREAKS, checked: three regressions in tests/test_bdio_seams_roots.py build a literal runner incidentally while testing a MISSING RESOLVED-CONFIG PIN. Each would start failing on the runner-pattern message instead of its intended message. Each retargets by keeping runner="profile:implementer" and stripping only the config pin. One test name becomes a misnomer and should be renamed. Nothing else found: instructions is not schema-required (required is name and kind only; ADR 0002 enforces it at create_root instead), so the two instructions regressions are unaffected.

COST: one canonical-serialize plus jsonschema validate per new-key create. Bounded, paid once per instance, and the same work already happens on the read side.

JUDGEMENT CALL to settle when actioning: this makes create_root reject bodies that GraphDefinition construction accepted, so the Pydantic model stays looser than the carrier. That is already true today via the post-write read; the change only makes it honest and non-destructive.

This is the third time this boundary surfaced today from unrelated directions -- the disciplines review (where a claim checker belongs), the cr-xb2 model-pin guard, and this. create_root is the real boundary and the validator is one layer too high.
close_reason: Merged 865b598. Root creation now validates and pins the body before writing: canonical bytes are re-validated through load_pinned_body, the declared hash is compared, and runner/model/effort are required for every task. Prevents a root whose every later read raises at parse_root. Reviewed Terra -> Opus 5 medium -> Sol high (SHIP). Merged-result gates all seven green: 1288 not-bd-not-live, 123 proc, 22 bd, 66 acceptance, ruff check+format clean, mypy --strict clean on 91 files.

title: A steer that crashes between close_activation and mint strands the instance forever
description:
Found by GPT-5.6 Sol on the cr-xb2 round 4 review. Distinct from cr-xb2: this is a recovery-lifecycle defect, not root-pin divergence, and the crash half is pre-existing.

Steerer.resume closes the parent (supervisor/steer.py:226) BEFORE the root read, the two pin reads, and the mint at :238-254. Anything that fails in that window -- a crash, a bd read failure, or pinned_execution_setting raising for a legacy root with no pins -- leaves a closed steered activation with no continuation.

Recovery cannot repair it. classify() discards the intent for closed lifecycles (supervisor/recover.py:229), so on re-entry route_head invokes recovery, receives no action, and returns no progress (foreman/cases.py:408). Ordinary ticks then repeat forever with no forward motion and no operator signal beyond the stall.

The resume docstring claims every step is idempotent so recovery can re-enter at an unknown crash point. That claim is FALSE for the close-to-mint window specifically. The close-forward repair it describes works for already-settled rows; it does not cover a settled row whose continuation was never minted.

Fix direction from Sol: make a closed steered head that still has a persisted intent re-enter the idempotent continuation mint when no continuation exists. Normalize the intent before the destructive work while retaining close-forward repair for already-settled rows.

Note the interaction with cr-xb2 round 5: once the creation guard covers every execution setting, the legacy-root trigger narrows to roots created before that guard. The crash trigger is unaffected and is the durable half of this bug.
close_reason: Merged 64e62b7. A fresh steer no longer destroys a running child for a refusal knowable beforehand: the race plan and supersede_activation now share _may_be_superseded, and the mint preflight shares the whole non-writing preparation. Four rounds (pins -> bounds -> race -> race predicate); each round found the prior fix modelled a subset of the real path. Residual is honest and structural: TOCTOU cannot be closed by a preflight. Reviewed Terra -> Opus 5 medium -> Sol high (SHIP, no findings). Merged-result gates all seven green.

title: Record which rules are load-bearing for build-loop's TDD, with enforcement tier per rule
description:
The v1-scoped half of the disciplines work. The discipline FRAMEWORK (library, claim checker, composition) is out of v1; this doc is what carries its value at near-zero cost.

build-loop enforces TDD through four mechanisms of descending strength, and nothing in the repo says which rule rests on which:

1. tick / topology -- ordering (write_tests before review_tests before implement)
2. bwrap mounts -- write scope via allowed_paths
3. pinned verifiers -- tests-untouched.sh, assertion-strength.sh, mutate.sh
4. prose -- node instructions, e.g. "each test must be able to fail"

The concrete risk this closes is already half-realised. implement allowed_paths was widened from tests/unit/** to tests/** for cr-o85.34.21, so the entire do-not-edit-your-own-yardstick rule migrated from a sandbox guarantee (tier 2) to a single verifier (tier 3). The comment at workflows/build-loop.toml:110-116 states this, but nothing declares that verifier load-bearing for a discipline. Delete it and the graph still validates, the hash moves, and TDD is silently prose-only.

Deliverable: a doc listing each rule that constitutes build-loop TDD, its tier, and the file:line that enforces it. It is also the artifact a future claim checker consumes, so keep it structured.

Related: cr-5fs (the recovery path that bypasses tier 1 entirely).

title: build-loop: every tests-region node's infra-retry fallback lands in triage_build, whose rebudget enters implement
description:
Traced in source, not reproduced live.

The tests region is bounded by on_exhausted = triage_tests, whose rebudget edge correctly returns to write_tests. That covers REGION_ROUNDS exhaustion only.

INFRA_RETRIES exhaustion takes a different route. foreman/bounds.py refusal_route uses node.fallback or index.document.fallback. review_tests declares no node-level fallback, so it falls through to the document fallback, which build-loop.toml sets to triage_build. foreman/cases.py then opens a transition gate on that node. triage_build outcomes are only rebudget and abandon, and its rebudget edge targets implement.

Result: if review_tests exhausts infrastructure retries, the only non-abandon option available to the human jumps straight to implement, having never obtained review_tests.accept. The test-first ordering that the graph otherwise enforces topologically is bypassed on this path.

It is not silent -- a human must open the gate. But the gate is named triage_build and its rebudget outcome reads as give the build more budget, not waive test review. The recovery vocabulary cannot express the correct action, which is resume test review.

Options: give review_tests a node-level fallback pointing at triage_tests; or widen the triage outcome set so a human can route back to the test region; or make the document fallback region-aware.

Found by GPT-6 Astra during the disciplines review and confirmed independently against bounds.py, cases.py and build-loop.toml.
notes:
SCOPE CORRECTION (Claude Fable 5.1, confirmed independently): this is a CLASS, not one node. Verified: the string fallback occurs exactly once in workflows/build-loop.toml -- the document-level [fallback] table. No node declares a node-level fallback. Since bounds.py refusal_route uses node.fallback or index.document.fallback for INFRA_RETRIES, EVERY tests-region task node (write_tests and review_tests) routes to triage_build on infra-retry exhaustion, and triage_build rebudget enters implement.

Astra traced it via review_tests; Fable traced it via write_tests. Same class, two instances.

Fix accordingly: a node-level fallback on every tests-region node pointing at triage_tests, not a patch to one node. Alternative framing worth considering: make the document fallback region-aware so the default is structurally correct rather than restated per node.

title: execution skill: the all-stages-closed discipline gate is unsatisfiable
description:
Found by an Opus 5 review of the bridge plan on 2026-09-07 and confirmed by measurement. .claude/skills/execution/SKILL.md:89-96 gates a phase close on: n=$(bd list --parent <epic> --json | jq length); u=$(unclosed count); [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && [ "$u" -eq 0 ]. But bd list --parent omits closed children unless --all is passed. Measured on the closed epic cr-o85.33: without --all it returns 0 rows, with --all it returns 12. So at the exact moment every child is closed, n becomes 0 and the gate fails its own n>0 precondition. The gate can never pass. This is independent of the bridge work; any phase closed through this skill either never hit the gate or it was overridden.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Take an epic whose children are all closed, e.g. cr-o85.33.
2. Run: bd list --parent cr-o85.33 --json | jq length  -> 0
3. Run: bd list --parent cr-o85.33 --all --json | jq length  -> 12
4. Substitute into the SKILL.md:89-96 gate: n=0, so [ "$n" -gt 0 ] is false and the phase cannot close.
acceptance_criteria: The gate counts closed children (--all or equivalent) so that a fully-closed epic passes and an epic with any unclosed child fails; a test or a worked example pins both directions.
close_reason: Fixed in 88bbb17. All three bd list --parent invocations in the phase-close gate now pass --all, with the reason stated inline so it is not simplified back out. title: Discipline composition: Node has no method or discipline-set field, so mount-many has no mechanism

title: Reconcile the spec, plans and tracker with the code that actually shipped

title: Durable acceptance matrix: map each of the 28 spec drills to its test and its execution evidence
description: GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07. Only 15 of the 28 spec section 13 drills carry a drill_N name in a test function; the rest are covered under descriptive names, so a grep understates coverage badly. But the opposite claim is also unsupported: no artifact maps drill to test to fresh execution evidence. Distinguish four classes explicitly: synthetic race residue, lab rebuild, real process crash, real vendor run. Rerun the full gate on a bwrap-capable host and archive sanitized evidence somewhere durable, not scratchpad.
