title: token_budget and trim_priority are declared and validated but never consumed — prompts are unbounded
description:
GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07, confirmed by orchestrator. schema/models.py:269 declares source trim_priority and rules_references.py:219 validates it is >= 1, but NO runtime consumer reads it. node.token_budget is threaded to TaskSpec (foreman/supervise.py:171) and profile.py:145 but nothing trims against it. inputs.py materializes every bound input whole: writing outputs become full diffs, non-writing outputs concatenate all output-tree files. A large diff or findings set therefore produces an unexpectedly large prompt with no ceiling. The graph calls token_budget a context-trim budget; today it is decoration.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Author a node with token_budget set and two sources at different trim_priority.
2. Run it where the bound inputs (a large diff, or an output tree with many files) exceed that budget.
3. Inspect the composed brief: every source is present whole, nothing was dropped or truncated.
4. Confirm statically: grep -rn trim_priority workflow_interpreter/ --include=*.py returns only the declaration (schema/models.py:269) and the validation rule (schema/rules_references.py:219). No consumer.
design: Decide first whether trim_priority is the mechanism or should be deleted. If kept, the composer drops or truncates lowest-priority sources until the brief fits token_budget, and records what it dropped in the activation so the trace shows it. Distinct from cr-o85.9, which is about tokens-vs-USD mapping, not prompt composition.
acceptance_criteria: A node with a token_budget and inputs exceeding it produces a brief within budget; the dropped or truncated sources are recorded on the activation; a test pins both the fit and the record. Or: trim_priority is deleted and the validation rule with it.
notes: Superseded by the owner-approved P2 UTF-8 context_budget_bytes contract: whole essential inputs, priority-based optional omission, actual envelope accounting and explicit legacy token_budget diagnostics. This is not exact token accounting; see P2 verification and cr-bwo.4.

title: [P1] Complete sequential execution
description: THE central vision gap, found independently by two audits (2026-09-07 Fable 5.1 + GPT-6 Astra). The engine sits BESIDE the harness workflow instead of under it: .claude/skills/execution/SKILL.md still selects, claims, executes and closes stages in prose, while both graphs start at implement/write_tests. docs/ideas/workflow-graphs.md:24 named replacing that prose as the whole point of the idea. Until one real multi-stage phase runs through wf create + wf run from the normal entry point, the interpreter is a parallel system nobody uses.
design: docs/specs/2026-09-11-workflow-coordination.md
acceptance_criteria: One real multi-stage roadmap phase completes through the interpreter, entered from /phase-execution, with no prose stage loop running in parallel; stage closure and gate rendering come from the graph; the run is reproducible from bd + git + the wrapper dir.
notes:
2026-09-07: plan v8 landed, docs/plans/phase-execution-interpreter-bridge.md, 488 lines. Eight Terra rounds, five review passes (Opus 5 medium x3, GPT-5.6 Sol high x2, GPT-6 Astra medium x1).

2026-09-09 MINIMALITY PASS — v8 superseded. All five prior reviews were adversarial CORRECTNESS reviews, which only ever add mechanism; none asked whether a mechanism was necessary. Fable 5.1 high asked that question and returned RESTRUCTURE; GPT-6 Astra high adversarially reviewed the rulings and returned ACCEPT WITH EXCEPTIONS (3). Reports in scratchpad/bridge-min/ (gitignored).

Core finding: the v8 landing core existed to make a TRUE MERGE safe against parallel landings. This repo is single-owner, single-machine, no CI, no other writers. Astra: confidence HIGH that concurrent merge/resolution machinery is unnecessary for criterion 1.

OWNER APPROVED 2026-09-09 — three ruling changes: (1) cut O1 cryptographic re-verification and ref re-dereference; (2) cut Stage 3, the conflict fixture, the interloper commit, the D11 resolution ceremony and the D10 counterfactual — the proof is TWO stages; (3) merge stage bead and source bead into ONE record. Also: keep the proof roadmap, no cleanup commit.

Three MANDATORY Astra corrections in v9: (C1) a full-gate receipt bound to the tested OID must be persisted BEFORE either close — a crash between merge and the first gate command would otherwise close both records with no verification at all; (C2) find_roots is lookup not repair — two concrete crash windows need a real repair path plus fault injection; (C3) --ff-only success does not prove artifact identity — an already-ancestor commit succeeds WITHOUT moving HEAD, so landing must classify fresh / replay / refuse.

Transport finding both models confirmed and five prior reviews missed: GitSubcommand excludes merge (supervisor/gitcmd.py:99-140). Neither v8 nor the ff-only replacement works through the unchanged transport. Resolution: a narrow bridge-local subprocess, bounded, preserving the transport timeouts and config hardening.

Stale in v8: the cr-dbk dependency (fixed 88bbb17 on 2026-09-08); D8 six dead-end kinds (now seven); two of three named source-bead candidates fail O2 eligibility.

Cost falls from 1.8-3.1 graph hours / $6-13 / three ceremonies to roughly 1.2 graph hours / $4-5 / two ceremonies, MINUS whatever the three corrections add back. Treat as a floor.
2026-09-11 owner approved the six-phase roadmap and resuming the paused worktree. Existing bridge defects remain in scope. Fable 5.1 high reviews after P1, P3, P5. No commits/main merge/push. Resume with execution and test-driven-development.

title: phase-5: test_steer_proc_raises_its_own_flag_and_kills_a_genuinely_live_child is load-sensitive — 2 failures in ~8 full-suite runs
description:
Observed 2026-09-02: the proc-marked steer test failed twice during the
cr-mub/cr-0zc work and passed on every other run — 3 consecutive clean
full-suite runs (984 passed) immediately after, plus 2 clean `-m proc` runs and
a clean single-test run, with no code change in between.

Both failures happened while other work was competing for the machine (the live
DRILL-27 rig had detached wrapper processes running). The test forks a REAL
child and asserts it is alive within a timing window, so scheduler pressure is
the obvious suspect.

Not diagnosed: the failure output was swallowed by the `-q` summary and the
test passed on every attempt to reproduce it, so there is no traceback. Do NOT
"fix" this by widening the window blind — the liveness assertion's PLACEMENT is
load-bearing (a mutation probe earlier in the same session showed the
assertion is dead if it sits after `await_barrier`, recorded in
.claude/project/learnings.md). Capture a real traceback first, under
`--tb=long` with the machine loaded.

Reproduction attempt: run the full suite with the live rig ticking in parallel.
notes:
2026-09-04 FIRST REAL TRACEBACK (phase-6 E2 live run, verify log /tmp/verify-feature.4079170.log, also failed 07:19 in review r1 of root wf-y6q and once in review r2 of wf-rjq):
  steer.py:202 steer -> steer.py:224 resume -> store.close_activation(STEERED) -> transitions.py:125
  LifecycleConflictError: activation wf-3 already recorded outcome error_transport at lifecycle closed
Sequence in the log: 07:18:29 child launched + stale flag mirrored; 07:18:30 wf.steer.session_pinned; then the conflict. So steer() ran within 1s of launch and lost a race: between its terminate() and its close_activation(STEERED), the forked WRAPPER's own monitor cycle observed the child dead and closed the activation as exit_unobserved -> error_transport (run.py _exit_reason fallthrough; monitor.py _unreapable_reason returns None when reaped.ours and no code). The wrapper never reads steer_intent (grep run.py/exit.py/monitor.py: no reader), so the intent written before the kill cannot make it defer; only foreman-side recovery (recover._case) honours STEER_PENDING. Under load the wrapper's cycle lands inside steer's kill->close window more often. This is a product race, not a timing-window test bug: the activation ends error_transport with a steer intent on disk, and the next tick's recovery finishes the steer. Fix candidates: (1) the wrapper's exit path checks steer_intent before grading and records ExitReason steered / defers the close; (2) steer() holds the wrapper's activation lock (wrapper.lock exists) across kill->close. Do NOT widen the test's window. Live consequence: this test sits in scripts/verify-feature.sh, so a flake at a review node is a fail_code rework round (cr-o85.34.13).
close_reason: Product race fixed: Supervisor._supervise reads steer-intent.json after monitor.watch and, if present, returns without observing the exit (no exit file, no record_exit, no close); the steerer or §5.6 STEER_PENDING recovery owns the close. Second cause found: the test's _runner_alive used bare /proc existence and saw the un-reaped zombie (~3% under load, identical before/after the wrapper fix); it now reads /proc/<pid>/stat and treats state Z as dead, placement unchanged. 30/30 loaded runs green. Gates 1054/70 tests, ruff, format, mypy green.

title: phase-4 DEFECT: snapshot_commit's 'git add --all' honours a runner-writable .gitattributes ⇒ repo-configured clean filters run as the wrapper over runner content (gitio.py:26-35 documented residual)
description: Surfaced by phase-5 planning (Sol r16 N1 on pin_outputs, fixed there with filter-free plumbing: hash-object --no-filters + update-index --cacheinfo). The §5.4 pre-destruction snapshot (workspace._pin_pre_reset → Git.snapshot_commit, gitio.py:445-477) still uses 'add --all' on the runner-dirtied tree; a runner that writes .gitattributes (writes=true nodes) can select any filter.<name>.clean present in the repo's .git/config (e.g. git-lfs), which executes as the wrapper and replaces the snapshotted bytes with the filter's output. Mitigation shape: enumerate (ls-files -z --others --modified --exclude-standard + deleted) then hash-object --no-filters + update-index --cacheinfo, or GIT_ATTR overrides where possible. Decision pending (user): fold into phase 5 as R8 or keep as a bead.
close_reason: Repaired in phase-5 slice A as §2b R8: snapshot_commit is filter-free plumbing — read-tree HEAD, ls-files -z --stage (gitlinks preserved verbatim, 160000), hash-object -w --no-filters, update-index --cacheinfo/--force-remove, write-tree, commit-tree. GitSubcommand.ADD greps to 0. Proven by test_a_runner_gitattributes_cannot_run_a_clean_filter, which plants a real filter.runner.clean and asserts the sentinel was never written and the runner's own bytes survived. Slice A accepted.

title: phase-5: an INFRA_RETRY of a steer-continuation must carry the steer forward (dispatch refuses it loudly for now)
description: Opus r3 #25. Dispatcher._steer_instructions keys on mint_reason == STEER_CONTINUATION only, so an infra retry minted at the same node with the continuation as predecessor would have relaunched with the node's ORIGINAL brief in a fresh session — the steer evaporating silently. Phase-4 closeout makes this fail-closed: an INFRA_RETRY whose predecessor is a STEER_CONTINUATION raises ContinuationRefused. Phase 5 must decide how the retry carries the steer (walk P→C→R to the intent file + reuse the pinned session id) and what session id the retry MintRequest carries.
close_reason: landed on followups-p1-p2 (critic APPROVE; minors fixed): dispatch persists prepare()'s id, mint hard-code deleted; infra retry of a steer continuation resumes the session with the steered activation's intent

title: DWS: worker lease validity uses wall clock; forward clock steps can raise lease_lost
description: Found by Sol high review 2026-10-07 (cr-gqbx round). jobs.py lease checks (_fence, heartbeat, publication) compare persisted UTC lease expiry with time.time(). A forward wall-clock step larger than the remaining lease (lease_seconds can be as low as 10) makes the live executor fail with non-retryable lease_lost. Pre-existing. WSL2 host observed ~9 s forward jumps; default lease_seconds=120 makes it unlikely in practice. Fix idea: measure live-lease validity monotonically within the owning process while keeping owner/epoch fencing and UTC for cross-process recovery.

title: Ledger follow-up: sessions/artifacts/usage tables have no writer; verify the cross-version-import item
description:
Lower-severity findings from the cr-3411 final epic review, kept together because each is small and none blocks merge. All verified in code.

1. sessions, artifacts and usage tables have no writer (Sol finding 4). They appear only in ledger/constants.py; only findings is written on close, and import rebuilds only findings. constants.py said 'the per-activation facts stay out until S4 writes them' and S4 wrote only findings — so this is a design-authority deviation, not data loss. ledger/export.py:_clear acknowledges the state in its own docstring.

2. Ledger root ids are minted from COUNT(roots WHERE task_id) and ignore the pinned attempt (Fable finding 3). ledger/store.py:735-738, rowmap.py:94,143-144,200. The D8/§2 child form <task>-a<n>-c<m> does not exist and parent_root_id is always NULL, so a composition child is minted as if it were an attempt and shifts the next real attempt's id. Latent today: feature-delivery has no composition.

3. archive_task deletes run folders without the tick's liveness guard and does not require the bridge record to be CLOSED (Sol finding 5, Fable finding 7). ledger/archive.py:72-107 versus foreman/tick.py:816-825. A crash between record_export_oid and the CLOSED merge leaves an open task that archive accepts.

4. _close_gate merges a carrier copied outside the transaction with no version check (Fable finding 5). ledger/store.py:437-438. The decision is safe because _decidable re-reads state; only stale_approval_receipts appended by a concurrent intake can be lost.

5. Import refuses any export whose schema_version differs, with no file-side upgrade path (Fable finding 6). ledger/export.py:377-387. Bites the next migration, not this one.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five is either fixed or explicitly accepted with a recorded rationale.

title: Durable monitor/wake in the foreman: heartbeat-driven wake-ups without a human or LLM polling
description:
Today the coordinator is the monitor. On 2026-09-15 every bridged stage needed a hand-written watch-*.py (Popen the driver, write a JSON heartbeat each minute from process state + run.jsonl mtime) plus a harness Monitor polling that heartbeat, re-armed every 30 minutes. That is LLM-and-human polling in the hot loop, the opposite of the LLM-in-the-loop principle (deterministic inner loop; judgment at seams).

Reference pattern: QM monitor poller (yc-software/qm e0b8686, src/monitors/monitor-poller.ts; comparison note in orchestrators/docs/research/agent-systems/comparison/qm-vs-workflow-interpreter.md). A durable monitor record stores a cursor and tail over a process output stream; a core poller (10 s) reads at most 64 KiB past the cursor and fires on new output, exit, TTL expiry, process loss, or a quiet heartbeat, with a minimum fire interval, max fires per tick, pattern filter, and idempotent fire keys; a fire enqueues a NEW turn rather than injecting into the live one. Borrow the pattern, not the code (their host is Postgres + Node; ours is bd + foreman tick).

Proposal for ours: (1) the foreman driver writes a heartbeat record (tick count, last event, current activation/gate, run.jsonl offset) on every tick; (2) a wake condition list on the instance: gate opened, root terminal, refusal written, driver exit, heartbeat stale > N; (3) when a condition fires, emit one durable wake event (bd event with an idempotent fire key = instance_key + condition + cursor) and run an optional host hook command (e.g. notify the coordinator session, or print a compact status) — never call a model; (4) a minimum fire interval and a per-instance cap so a flapping driver cannot spam; (5) compact status output that the coordinator reads instead of transcripts.

Out of scope: injecting into a running activation, any LLM call in the poller, multi-replica leader leases.
acceptance_criteria: Running phase-bridge on a stage and walking away yields exactly one durable wake event per gate opening, one on terminal, one on refusal, and one on stale heartbeat, each with an idempotent fire key; re-running the poller does not duplicate events; a host hook command receives the compact status; unit tests cover cursor advance, dedupe, min-fire-interval, and stale detection with a stub driver; no model is invoked anywhere in the path.

title: Bind crew identity into LaunchReceipt so inspector reattachment cannot adopt a foreign vendor
description:
Deferred from cr-xb2 round 4. Found by GPT-5.6 Sol, shape corrected by Opus 5; both verified independently.

supervisor/launch.py _reattach returns the durable receipt when receipt.state is STARTED and ledger.has_launch(receipt.launch_id), with NO comparison of which vendor the receipt describes, and dispatch then bypasses _launch. A pre-fix wrapper could launch the metadata-selected vendor, write receipt plus ledger line, and die before record_dispatch, leaving the activation MINTED. A post-fix wrapper then adopts that still-running foreign process, and supervisor/run.py observes its output through the root-selected profile.

Legacy-only: post-cr-xb2 no launch can write a receipt whose vendor differs from the root pin, because create_root freezes the resolution and _assert_same_instance makes it immutable per instance key.

SHAPE, corrected from Sols original proposal:
- No normalizer needed. Profile.name already returns the bare RunnerName value and _launch already holds profile. Store a plain str or None.
- Do NOT import profiles into supervisor -- profiles/registry.py imports supervisor.profile, so that direction is a cycle. Compare against the profile dispatch was handed.
- Follow the sandbox: SandboxMode = OFF precedent at supervisor/models.py:300 -- a defaulted flagging value whose only reachable source is a receipt from a launcher predating the field.
- CRITICAL: None means UNKNOWN, not foreign, and most such receipts describe the correct vendor. Mismatch (not None and != profile.name) should terminate/settle/halt. None should REFUSE TO ADOPT with a typed operator-readable refusal, ideally recording a deviation -- NOT kill. Sol proposed killing on None, which would destroy legitimate crash-window work on the first upgrade-straddling activation.
- Do not let the mismatch branch fall through to the existing ExecLedgerError path: it fails closed but blames an unexplained ledger line, and leaves the foreign child running with no max_wall and no exit record, which is the exact harm adoption exists to prevent.
- RECORD_MODEL is extra=forbid, so a new receipt read by an old binary parses as malformed; only matters on rollback.

RELATED, worth its own bead: the root pins a runner NAME, not an executable. ProfileConfig carries per-vendor binary overrides resolved from live config at profile_for time, so two wrappers under different config can exec different binaries for the same pinned name -- and a receipt field storing profile.name would see no mismatch.

title: spike-then-harden is not expressible: no base-commit lineage primitive
description:
Found by Claude Fable 5.1 during the disciplines review; the largest of the gaps it named.

Spike-then-harden as a discipline means: explore freely in a spike, then harden by building on the PRE-SPIKE base with the spike diff as read-only knowledge. Its defining rule is lineage.

That rule cannot be stated today. intended_base_commit is a derived mint fact -- spec section 3.2 fixes it as the predecessor pre_attempt_commit on rework, else the instance branch head -- and mint facts are never caller-supplied. A forward edge from spike to harden therefore bases harden on the spike artifact, which is exactly what the discipline forbids.

Prose cannot substitute. An instruction saying "revert the spike first" cannot reset a base commit, and a reviewer cannot distinguish a genuine hand-revert from partial salvage of spike code.

What is needed is a pinned-body primitive, e.g. a per-node base = "predecessor_base". That is admissible under the mint-facts-are-derived rule, because the graph body is pinned data rather than a caller parameter -- the derivation stays fixed, the body selects which fixed derivation applies.

Until such a primitive exists, do NOT claim spike-then-harden via node instructions. It would be a discipline the system advertises and cannot enforce.

Blocked on the disciplines mechanism decision. Do not action standalone.
notes: Deferred 2026-09-21 with cr-o85.43: graph-language feature waiting on the disciplines ruling (out of v1, 2026-09-08).

title: No outcome in the closed enum can carry escalate-on-doubt
description:
Found during the disciplines review (Astra + Fable, independently).

Escalate-on-doubt as a discipline needs a node to emit a verdict meaning "I am not confident, route me elsewhere". The outcome enum is closed and has no such value, so any graph expressing it must overload an existing outcome -- in practice fail_plan.

That collides structurally: schema rule 4 permits exactly one edge per (from, outcome) pair. build-loop already routes implement --fail_plan--> triage_build. A doubt discipline wanting implement --fail_plan--> consult cannot coexist with it. Reviewers also already read fail_plan as "abandon this plan", so overloading it is semantically wrong as well as structurally blocked.

Adding a distinct outcome is a schema addition, not a migration: exclude_none emission leaves every existing graph byte-identical, so no pinned body or content hash moves.

Related and separate: escalate-AFTER-N-attempts is a different feature and is NOT expressible either, because on_exhausted must target a gate and gate_type is closed to human. ADR 0004 defers gate_type = model with a trigger. So the feasible form is escalate-when-the-node-says-so, i.e. the node holds the verdict, consistent with ADR 0004.

Blocked on the disciplines mechanism decision. Do not action standalone.

title: Legacy divergent activations settle on metadata runner while launching the pinned one
description:
cr-xb2 closed the launch half of runner divergence: run_wrapper now selects the profile from the root-resolved node. Settlement was deliberately left reading activation metadata (foreman/cases.py:320 and :341), which is correct in general -- replay must parse the output of the vendor that actually ran.

Likely surfaces as a replay mismatch halt gate rather than silent corruption, but the EXIT_RECORDED branch has no prior evidence to compare against, so that is unverified.

Decide: migration/backfill for pre-guard activations, or a settlement-time consistency check that halts explicitly.

title: re-verification stamps have no expiry, so a merge can silently invalidate them
description:
Process gap found 2026-09-08 during the post-cr-cwq bead review.

On 2026-09-07 a read-only audit re-verified ~22 deferred beads against commit ab84e58 and stamped each with: "RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (gpt-5.6-terra high, read-only audit vs code at ab84e58): STILL-VALID. Evidence: <file:line>. Do not re-audit this against the code without new reason."

That stamp is good practice — it names the commit, cites evidence, and stops re-litigation. It has one hole: nothing detects when a NEW REASON has arrived.

Measured instance. The cr-cwq merge (912ef93) landed one commit after ab84e58 and invalidated two beads carrying that exact stamp, both dated the previous day: cr-o85.8 (TaskSpec has no effort field — cr-cwq added TaskSpec.effort at supervisor/profile.py:140) and cr-o85.13 (a per-vendor default model table belongs with the role map — superseded by cr-49v). A re-audit of the other 16 in the same family found all 16 still valid, so the stamp was right 16 times out of 18 — but the two failures were invisible until someone re-read them by hand.

The general shape: a stamp asserts a fact about code at a commit, and a later merge touching those files is precisely the new reason the stamp asks for, yet the stamp cannot know a merge happened.

## Scope sketch

Record the files a stamp depends on, not only the commit — the evidence citations already name them. Then a check can ask whether any of those paths changed since the stamped commit and flag the bead for re-verification. bd notes already carry the commit and the file:line, so the data is present and unparsed.

## Acceptance criteria

Given a bead whose re-verification note cites file:line evidence at a commit, a command reports whether any cited file has changed since that commit, and lists which beads need re-verification. Demonstrated against the real case: cr-o85.8 and cr-o85.13 flagged after 912ef93, the other 16 in that family not flagged.

title: harden create_root against incomplete role pins, and rule on the vendor-default sentinel
description:
Split out of cr-cwq on 2026-09-08 by an Opus 5 adjudication of a GPT-5.6 Sol finding. Two related leftovers, both deliberately deferred.

## 1. create_root does not validate role pins

bdio/roots.py:121 checks only "if not resolved_config" — non-empty. It never requires a usable model and effort per task role. Reproduced: a resolved_config pinning a real model on node.implement with NO effort key at all was accepted, and resolved_node then yielded effort=None.

cr-cwq closed this class at the argv boundary (adapters refuse rather than omit) and at resolved_node (role-scoped refusal), which together make the dispatch path safe. Validating at create_root would additionally stop a bad root from ever being persisted.

It was NOT made primary deliberately: it pushes task-role config semantics into the config-agnostic bdio layer and would triplicate the definition of "what is a task role". Belt-and-suspenders, wrong layer to lead with.

## 2. Policy ruling on MODEL_VENDOR_DEFAULT

The sentinel means "omit the model flag and let the CLI pick". After cr-cwq the reproducibility contract says a root pins exactly one model per role and either the CLI runs it or the activation fails. Those two statements are in tension.

The sentinel survives today only as a graph-authoring placeholder: both shipped graphs set model = "default" in their node bodies, and _resolved_config overwrites any graph-default model with the role binding real model before it reaches a TaskSpec. Every task node is role-bound by schema (graph_schema.json:185 admits a profile:<role> alias only), so no task node can reach dispatch still carrying the sentinel.

The ruling needed: does the sentinel keep any legitimacy for task roles, or is it retired — with the shipped graphs dropping their model = "default" lines, since the schema makes the field optional and the role binding supplies it regardless.

## Acceptance criteria

create_root refuses a resolved_config whose task role lacks a usable model or effort, with a test in both directions. The sentinel question is answered in an ADR or a comment at MODEL_VENDOR_DEFAULT, and the shipped graphs match the ruling.

title: Record the served model set (result.modelUsage) on ActivationMetadata, not only in cost reports
description:
Split out of cr-cwq on 2026-09-08. Independent of fallback: it turns a pinned model from a CLAIM into a VERIFIED FACT.

cr-cwq pins model and effort per role into the immutable root. Nothing checks that the CLI honoured the pin. If a vendor silently substitutes, ignores an unknown alias, or routes to a different tier, the root still asserts the pinned model and no evidence contradicts it.

Measured by an Opus 5 review of the claude stream fixtures on 2026-09-08 — the served model is already present in the stream the profile parses, in three places:
- the system/init line carries "model" (tests/fixtures/profiles/claude/tools.jsonl:1, resume.jsonl:1)
- every assistant event carries message.model (tools.jsonl:3,4,8)
- the terminal result line carries modelUsage, an object keyed by every canonical model that actually consumed tokens, with per-model tokens and cost. The fixtures show TWO distinct models keyed in one run (result.json:1, live-result.jsonl:1), which is what makes this surface definitive rather than indicative.

modelUsage is the strongest surface: terminal, definitive, and it enumerates every served model by name.

## Scope

Thread a served-model field from the result event through RunnerEvent, LogScan and TerminalEnvelope (all three currently drop it) onto ActivationMetadata (bdio/wire.py:343-382, which today carries only the pinned model plus usage).

## Acceptance criteria

An activation whose CLI reports modelUsage records the served model set on its metadata; a mismatch between the pinned model and the served set is visible to a reader of the activation without re-reading logs. Decide deliberately whether a mismatch should also fail the activation and record the reasoning.

title: probe-driven model substitution ignores an overridden fallback_models chain
description:
Found by the Opus 5 critic on the cr-cwq round-1 diff, 2026-09-08.

foreman/resolve.py:439-451. NodeSetting.FALLBACK_MODELS was added to TASK_SETTING_TYPES (resolve.py:70-71), so the fallback chain is settable by project-config and instance-override. Claude honours such an override: its --fallback-model flows from the resolved setting through ResolvedNode.fallback_models into the TaskSpec. The codex/opencode probe does not — _available_model picks its substitute from binding.fallback, the raw TOML role binding, never from the resolved setting.

Failure scenario: an operator sets node.implement.fallback_models = "modelX" in project-config for a codex-bound role whose primary probe fails. The root records fallback_models = modelX, but the model actually pinned is the first available entry of the original TOML fallback list. The recorded chain and the used chain diverge silently, and the root is the artefact an auditor reads.

Deferred deliberately from cr-cwq: overriding a fallback chain was outside that bead brief, and the critic rated it narrow.

## Acceptance criteria

_available_model reads the resolved fallback chain rather than the raw binding, so an overridden chain drives the probe; a test sets fallback_models via project-config on a codex role with a failing primary probe and asserts the pinned model comes from the override.
close_reason: Superseded: owner decided 2026-09-08 to remove the fallback mechanism entirely rather than fix its override divergence. No fallback chain means nothing to override.

title: design-spec graph needs a domain-specific (non-coding) verifier

Two coding loops do not test that hypothesis. A research graph has different artifacts (findings, sources, a written doc), different verification (citations resolve, claims are sourced) and different gates than an implement/review loop.
design: Pick one real research or architecture task from the backlog rather than inventing a fixture. The point is to discover which parts of the engine assume a diff-producing writer node. Expect the effects gate, artifact pinning and the verify contract to need work for a node whose output is prose.

title: Legacy uncoordinated roots: execution band keyed on wrapper_home, not repo
description:
GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07, confirmed. foreman/config.py:42 builds wrapper_root from wrapper_home plus a hash of the repo path; owner.py:23 stores the ownership record inside that root; compose.py:160 creates the execution band from its paths. Spec section 4 says the band is one active runner ever for a repo, but the lock identity includes wrapper_home. Two configurations pointing different wrapper homes at the same checkout get two independent bands and can run two runners against one working tree. Spec section 14 documents this as a known siting deviation; no issue tracked resolving it.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Point one foreman config at wrapper_home A and a second at wrapper_home B, both over the same repo checkout.
2. Start an instance under each.
3. Both acquire a band and dispatch: the flock paths differ because they are derived under different wrapper roots, so neither excludes the other.
design: Blocking for concurrency work: leases and merge slots assume the band is authoritative per repo. Either derive the band path from the canonicalized repo identity alone, or refuse to start when another wrapper root already claims the repo.
acceptance_criteria: Two wrapper homes over one checkout cannot both hold the band; the second refuses with a message naming the holder; a test pins it.

title: Deferred phase-7 verify checks have prose triggers and no work items

Each defers on a condition stated only in plan prose, e.g. wait until a malformed findings file occurs. No issue carries those triggers, so nothing will ever surface them and they can stay deferred indefinitely.
design: Do NOT build the checks now; the deferral reasoning is sound. File the triggers so they are observable: what artifact convention would unblock rows-vs-names, and what observed failure would justify the other two.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three deferred checks has a work item naming its observable trigger and the evidence that would justify building it; the phase-7 plan points at them instead of carrying the condition in prose.

title: build-loop red-test evidence is model-recorded, never mechanically checked
description:
GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07, confirmed by reading the graph and script. workflows/build-loop.toml:38,49 instruct write_tests to produce tests that fail for the right reason, but its verifier scripts/checks/tests-parse.sh only COLLECTS tests; it never runs them against the absent implementation. review_tests adds assertion detection, not execution. So the red phase rests entirely on reviewer judgement.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On the build-loop tests region, have write_tests emit a test file whose assertions already pass against the current tree (for example asserting something existing code already satisfies).
2. Run the node verify set: tests-parse.sh collects the tests and passes.
3. review_tests assertion-strength.sh finds assert statements and passes.
4. The tests region completes with no evidence any test ever failed.
design: Decide first whether observed red is REQUIRED evidence or advisory. If required, the check must distinguish an intended assertion failure from an import or setup error, otherwise a broken test file grades as a good red. That distinction is the hard part and the reason this was not built with the other four scripts.
acceptance_criteria: A tests-region node either produces recorded evidence that its tests ran and failed for an assertion reason, or the graph documents red as reviewer-judged and stops claiming it mechanically.

title: phase-5: foreman status surfaces only open HALT gates, never open TRANSITION gates — a waiting ship gate can be invisible
description: Found 2026-09-02 while adjudicating the round-2 6a disagreement. VERIFIED BY CODE READ: foreman/__main__.py:218-241 builds the status payload with root_id, activations, instance_base_commit, instance_branch_head, stale, and — only if frontier.open_halt is not None — open_halt. It never reports frontier.open_gates, which frontier.py:243 already computes and returns. Meanwhile foreman/tick.py:299 returns TickReport(terminal=...) on the fall-through path with NO opened_gate. CONSEQUENCE: a transition gate (e.g. the ship gate, GateReason.TRANSITION) is announced by exactly ONE TickReport.opened_gate, at the tick that opens it, and never again by any surface. A human who misses that single report — or whose foreman crashed in the 6a window before it was emitted (cr-hmm) — has no CLI signal that a gate is waiting for a signed decision. The instance is not stuck in any state the code considers wrong; it is simply invisible. NOT 6a-specific: the crash only guarantees the report is missed. This is the general case. SUGGESTED FIX: include frontier.open_gates in the status payload the same way open_halt is included, with the inbox path and payload template per gate. NOTE the interaction with cr-hmm: if status listed open transition gates, the delayed-backfill gap would be audit-only, which is what the round-2 brief provisionally assumed it already was.
acceptance_criteria: foreman status reports every open gate, not only halt gates, with enough detail for a human to submit a signed payload; a drill asserts a transition gate is discoverable on a tick AFTER the one that opened it.
notes:
REVERSED (2026-09-02, same session). The P1 escalation above was WRONG on two
counts, and the reversal is evidence-based.

1. There is NO notification requirement in the spec. The word "notification"
   occurs exactly ONCE in docs/specs/workflow-interpreter.md, at :863, and it
   is a WINDOW MARKER naming where the 6a crash lands — not a contract. The
   actual 6a requirement is the clause's own predicate: "re-tick converges, no
   duplicate gate (same key), no duplicate edge."
2. Spec:729 is explicit: **"Gates wait indefinitely in v1."** Waiting is the
   designed state, not a stall.

And the gate is NOT invisible. `bdio/gates.py:221-224` creates it as a durable
bd bead with a human-readable title (`_TITLE_GATE.format(gate_node, seq)`) and
logs `wf.gate.opened`. It is discoverable by `bd list --status=open` — the
issue tracker IS this system's durable store, and is exactly where a human is
expected to find waiting work. `foreman status` omitting open transition gates
is a UX nicety, which is what this bead is now scoped to.

Spec 6a is moreover ALREADY ASSERTED END TO END at
tests/test_foreman_e2e.py:292-359: converges (`opened_gate is None`, :314), no
duplicate gate (`len(lab.beads("gate")) == 1`, :340), no duplicate edge
(`events_backfilled == 2` then unchanged on re-tick, :356-359). The missed
event is backfilled exactly once at the next routing tick.

Sol's BLOCKER 1 does not survive the spec text. Fable's ruling stands. My own
"silent stall" escalation was an overclaim of the same species S1 exists to
catch, committed while adjudicating S1. Recorded here deliberately.

Re-scoped P1 -> P3, defect -> enhancement: make `foreman status` report
`frontier.open_gates` (frontier.py:243 already computes it) so a waiting
transition gate is visible without a `bd list`.
close_reason: FIXED. foreman/__main__.py status now reports open_gates — every OPEN gate, halt and transition alike — each with gate_id, node, reason, its inbox path and its unsigned payload template. open_halt kept unchanged for existing consumers. Test: tests/test_foreman_main.py::test_status_reports_an_open_transition_gate_with_its_inbox_and_template. Mutation-proven: filtering the new list back to HALT gates only (the exact pre-fix defect) turns the test RED. Motivation is operational, not the earlier 'silent stall' reasoning: status is the ONLY command that renders a gate inbox and payload template, and the shipped feature-delivery graph's ship and triage gates are both gate_type=human TRANSITION gates — so the live DRILL-27 acceptance (cr-o85.32) could not be driven by a human without this.

title: phase-5: a transition event missed by a 6a-window crash is NOT redelivered on re-tick — it waits for the next routing decision
description: Found by S1 batch 7 (2026-09-02) when injection point 6a was finally injected where the spec says: between gate persistence and its first notification. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: Foreman.tick() calls _backfill ONLY in the abandoned_halt branch (tick.py:272) and the head-routing branch (tick.py:277). Not in the dead_end branch, not in the empty/entry-mint branch, and not on the gate-intake path, which returns earlier. CONSEQUENCE: after a crash in the 6a window the gate bead has landed but its transition event has not, and the immediate re-tick backfills NOTHING (events_backfilled == 0) because the landed gate already consumes its source activation, so no routing decision remains to trigger the sweep. The event stays durably absent — never duplicated — until the next tick that takes ANY routing decision; in the drill that is the tick routing the closed ship gate to terminal, which then writes both outstanding events at once (events_backfilled == 2). An instance parked at an open gate awaiting a human keeps the event missing for that entire period. SPEC GAP: docs/specs/workflow-interpreter.md:861-863 says 'crash between gate-open and first notification ... => re-tick converges', which reads as immediate. It does not converge on re-tick. NOT yet classified as a correctness defect: events are a derived audit projection (bdio/bounds.py ceiling_count docstring excludes them) and nothing in routing reads them, so this looks like an audit-completeness and spec-wording gap rather than a control-flow bug. NEEDS A RULING: is delayed backfill the intended contract for anything downstream that watches transition events to know a transition occurred? The test now asserts the ACTUAL behaviour (0, 0, then 2) rather than the row's implied shape.
acceptance_criteria: Either the spec text is corrected to describe delayed backfill, or _backfill is called on the paths that currently skip it and the drill asserts immediate convergence.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN SUBSTANCE by the cr-tl3 adjudication (round-2 sign-off).

This bead was filed as "6a leaves a transition event unbackfilled". That half is
NOT a defect: `_backfill` runs on the next edge-taking tick (tick.py:277), so
the event is reconstructed once the gate's payload is submitted. Spec §3.3:475
defines events as an idempotently reconstructible audit projection, which this
satisfies. The gap is audit latency bounded by the gate's lifetime.

The REAL defect the 6a analysis exposed is notification, not backfill, and it
lives on cr-tl3 (raised to P1). Close this one in favour of cr-tl3 unless the
latency itself is judged unacceptable.

Earlier correction retained: "nothing in routing reads events" is FALSE —
frontier.py:141-161 reads TERMINAL events for `terminal` and consumption.
close_reason: Not a defect. The 6a event gap is audit latency bounded by the gate's lifetime, and spec 3.3:475 defines events as an idempotently reconstructible audit projection. Already asserted end to end at tests/test_foreman_e2e.py:292-359, including the exactly-once backfill at the next routing tick. See cr-tl3 for the reversal record.

title: phase-5: a §8.1 continuation's §5.4 precondition resets away the steered runner's uncommitted work (R1 consequence, probed)
description:
Reachable for the first time now that R1 makes a steer continuation dispatchable through Supervisor.run. Probed on a real worktree, real steer, real continuation:

  before steer, worktree holds: ['half-done.txt', 'scripts', 'src']
  continuation lifecycle: exit-recorded
  after continuation, worktree holds: ['scripts', 'src']
  reset_applied: True
  prereset refs: ['refs/wf/wf-1/prereset/wf-3']

Supervisor.run runs the same 5.4 precondition for a continuation as for any other activation. In worktree mode Workspace._plan takes snapshot=None, so every dirty path is 'resettable' with no attribution test, and _apply resets to intended_base_commit. The work is NOT lost — _pin_pre_reset commits and pins the whole dirty state first, under the CONTINUATION's activation id (refs/wf/<root>/prereset/<continuation>) — but the continuation's runner starts from a clean tree, not from where the steered runner left off.

Whether that is right is a spec question, not a defect: 8.1 says a steer continues a SESSION, and 5.4 says every dispatch proves a clean tree against its intended base. A continuation resuming a vendor session whose working tree has been reset under it is at least surprising. Phase 5 should settle it: either 8.1 continuations skip the reset (and 5.4 gains an exception with a reason), or the reset stays and 8.1 documents that a steer costs the uncommitted tree, recoverably. Probe: scratchpad/probes/phase4-cli-probes.md-adjacent scratch script probe_continuation_reset2.py. Nothing in phase 4 routes on either answer.

title: bdio: two closers on one activation are last-writer-wins inside the same §0.3 cooperative window (Opus#18, r4; api.py close_activation — both closes pass the is_settled guard on their own read, and the second merge overwrites the first outcome; bd has no compare-and-set, so the residue is documented §0.3 behaviour rather than a defect; probe scratchpad/probes/p3-r4-probes/probe_a_close_merge_window.py)
description:
bdio: two closers on one activation resolve last-writer-wins, so the recorded outcome is decided by merge ordering rather than by which close landed first.

## Mechanism

BdClient.close_activation (bdio/api.py:466) loads the record (:502), checks is_superseded (:503) and is_settled (:511) on ITS OWN read, then calls _apply(... lifecycle=CLOSED, outcome=...) at :524. _apply routes to transitions.apply, which re-reads fresh and re-runs assert_not_settled (transitions.py:234-235) before the unguarded _merge_metadata at :243.

The fresh re-read NARROWS the load-to-merge interval but cannot eliminate it, and bd offers no compare-and-set — stated at transitions.py:18.

## Failure scenario

Two closers on activation X carrying different outcomes: A with outcome=done, B with outcome=steered.

1. A apply fresh-reads X — not settled — passes assert_not_settled.
2. B apply fresh-reads X — A merge has not landed yet, still not settled — passes.
3. A merges lifecycle=closed outcome=done.
4. B merges lifecycle=closed outcome=steered, overwriting A outcome.

The recorded outcome is the section 3.3 routing truth a continuation is minted from, so a later activation is routed off whichever close merged last. Section 5.1 says the RECORDED close wins; this makes that ordering-dependent.

## Still true

Verified at 912ef93 (2026-09-08): close_activation guards on its own read (api.py:511) and apply re-guards on a fresh read (transitions.py:234), but the interval from :234 to the merge at :243 is unguarded and bd still offers no CAS.

## Acceptance criteria

Either the close performs a compare-and-set on the outcome and lifecycle keys so the first recorded outcome wins deterministically and the second closer is refused with a conflict, or the residue is documented as accepted section 0.3 cooperative-window behaviour citing scratchpad/probes/p3-r4-probes/probe_a_close_merge_window.py, asserting that in production a single foreman tick owns the close so two concurrent closers cannot arise by construction. Either way a test drives two different-outcome closers through the real api into one activation and asserts the chosen semantics.

The fresh-read guard narrows but cannot eliminate the interval before metadata merge; Bd still has no compare-and-set. Do not re-audit this against the code without new reason; it was checked at this commit.

title: bdio: repair_forward's own read-modify-write window can undo a write that landed between the read-back and the repair (Opus#17, r4; transitions.py:217 — decides the terminal lifecycle from the merge's read-back snapshot, then issues a SECOND bd update; a §3.2 supersede landing in between is written over by a decision taken before it existed; probe scratchpad/probes/p3-r4-probes/probe_d_repair_forward_race.py)
description:
bdio: repair_forward re-derives a terminal lifecycle from a STALE snapshot and writes it without re-reading, so it can undo a settle that landed in between — re-creating the inconsistency it exists to repair.

## Mechanism

bdio/transitions.py:243-244 — apply() merges the transition keys, then hands the merge READ-BACK to repair_forward. repair_forward (:247-272) decides the terminal lifecycle purely from that stale snapshot: terminal = SUPERSEDED if metadata.is_superseded else CLOSED (:260), guarded only by "if metadata.lifecycle is terminal: return" (:261). On mismatch it issues a SECOND _merge_metadata(record_id, {KEY_LIFECYCLE: terminal.value}) at :270-272.

There is no fresh re-read and no assert_not_settled between the read-back at :244 and that second write at :271 — unlike apply() itself, which re-loads and re-guards at :234-235.

## Failure scenario

Activation X. Thread A runs a transition through apply; its merge read-back S shows outcome != None, is_superseded=False, and a non-terminal lifecycle, so A computes terminal=CLOSED. Before A reaches :271, thread B lands a section 3.2 supersede writing lifecycle=superseded, outcome=steered, superseded_by=...

A then executes its second merge {lifecycle: closed}, dragging lifecycle back to closed on top of B row. Because repair_forward writes ONLY KEY_LIFECYCLE, B outcome=steered survives — producing exactly the status=closed lifecycle=closed outcome=steered inconsistency repair_forward exists to prevent, now created BY repair_forward, with B lifecycle=superseded silently undone.

## Still true

Verified at 912ef93 (2026-09-08): transitions.py:247-272 still computes terminal from the handed-in record.metadata and performs the second merge with no intervening fresh load or settle guard.

## Acceptance criteria

repair_forward re-reads fresh and re-guards immediately before its second merge, or refuses when the row already carries a strictly more terminal lifecycle. A test that interleaves a supersede into the read-back-to-repair window shows the supersede lifecycle=superseded is not overwritten. Alternatively the window is documented as accepted section 0.3 behaviour, citing scratchpad/probes/p3-r4-probes/probe_d_repair_forward_race.py as evidence.
acceptance_criteria: repair_forward either re-guards before its second metadata merge or documents the window as accepted §0.3 behaviour with the probe as evidence; a supersede landing between the read-back and the repair is not silently overwritten.
notes: Triage 2026-09-21: still real on LedgerStore; bdio/transitions.py:345-370 second lifecycle merge has no guard=.

title: bdio: package modules reach into BdClient._merge_metadata / _create_bead / _close_bead
description: roots.py, gates.py, canary.py, finalize.py, api.py, supervision.py and transitions.py all call the transport's package-private write methods. That IS the established convention — the methods are private to keep them off the PUBLIC surface (§0.1), not off sibling modules — and ruff's default rule set has no SLF001, so nothing flags it. Worth a decision rather than a drift: either name the convention in the package docstring or give the transport an explicit package-internal facade. Ruled Debt-OK by both r3 critics.

title: supervisor: ExitObserver reaches PinOutcome.REFUSED indirectly
description: At a normal exit ExitObserver calls Workspace.pin_artifact with quarantine=False, so an unattributable in-repo commit yields identity=None and §7 grades fail_code via 'done claim produced no commit; that is no_diff (§7.4)'. Safe — the commit is still HEAD so nothing is unreachable, and the refusal is logged at error — but the outcome is reached by an unrelated clause rather than by naming the refusal, and the reason string pin_artifact computed never reaches the evidence. Ruled Debt-OK by both r3 critics.

title: supervisor: Monitor.watch holds on INDETERMINATE with no ceiling
description: Monitor.watch returns only on a TERMINAL verdict, and INDETERMINATE (liveness unanswerable, or a max_wall termination that could not prove death) is deliberately non-terminal — holding position is the point (§5.6: absence of evidence is not evidence of death). But there is no ceiling on how long it holds, so a permanently unreadable /proc wedges a resident supervisor until a human ends it. Needs a policy decision first: what a wrapper should DO after N minutes of unanswerable liveness, given that recording an exit is exactly what must not happen. Ruled Debt-OK by both r3 critics.

title: bdio: recorded_precondition raises a raw ValidationError on an out-of-band trio
description: ActivationMetadata.pre_attempt_commit/reset_verified_commit are unvalidated str|None, so a bd row whose §3.2 trio was written out-of-band (hand-edit, older tool, direct bd update) makes bdio.supervision.recorded_precondition construct a PreconditionRecord that fails the CommitOid pattern. ValidationError is not a BdioError, so no caller catches it — a crash path on a READ. Probed: recorded_precondition(metadata with pre_attempt_commit='deadbeef') -> ValidationError. Fix means validating ActivationMetadata's commit fields, which was outside the phase-3 wire.py scope (PreconditionRecord + StaleFlagRecord only). Ruled Debt-OK by both r3 critics.

title: Command: sync -> rescan -> diff -> re-analyse -> recommend
description:
Turn the harness-evaluate skill (or a new command) into a single invocation that chains the whole reference-harness loop:

1. Sync reference_harnesses submodule pins to upstream HEAD.
2. Re-run scan.py to refresh catalogs/, then export_csv.py to refresh inventory/.
3. Diff against the previous catalogs: which skills are new, changed, or gone.
4. For changed/new skills only, run the consolidation analysis (see docs/plans/skill-consolidation-plan.md and the casebook) against the current adopted roster.
5. Output a recommendation per affected skill: ADD (new capability we lack), UPDATE (upstream now better than our adopted version), DOWNGRADE/REPLACE (our pick is no longer the best), or NO-CHANGE.
6. Append the new round to the casebook; never rewrite prior rounds.

Prerequisite: the casebook append-only log must exist first (harness_lifecycle/casebook/). Do not build until the casebook schema has settled through at least one manual round.

Deferred by user 2026-08-11 — recorded as an idea, not scheduled.
acceptance_criteria: One command runs sync, rescan, diff, re-analyse and recommend in order; a run with no upstream change reports no recommendations and changes no ledger entry.
